Senses.Note: The four settings have different current frames. The X82 hall talk belongs to Lingyan Yuanri, not Chuici Pushao; its exact heading governs the utterance. In T47 the questioner voices the inherited formula and Xuedou answers it. The J39 formula remains Zhaozhou's old reply within Yuanjie Jingying's separate appraisal. No lamp tier is promoted and no common original author is inferred.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：悟無不悟，得無不得，九年面壁空勞力。三脚驢兒跳上天，泥牛入海無蹤跡。為甚如此？九九八十一揑跳。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X82/X82n1571.xml). Under the explicit heading for Lingyan Yuanri in Fuzhou, the lamp records a hall talk juxtaposing awakening and attainment with nine years facing a wall, a three-legged donkey leaping to heaven and a clay ox disappearing into the sea. Yuanri asks why it is so and closes with the numerical formula and the following movement word. The local heading assigns this speech to Yuanri, correcting the earlier Chuici Pushao attribution. The multiplication follows this deliberately improbable sequence rather than supplying an independently explained numerical doctrine.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。承古有言。九九八十一。意旨如何。師云。金剛合掌。進云。學人不會。師云。歸依佛法僧。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1996.xml). An unnamed monk asks Xuedou Chongxian about the meaning of the old saying nine times nine is eighty-one. Xuedou replies with vajra palms joined. The monk says he does not understand, and Xuedou answers by taking refuge in Buddha, Dharma and Sangha. The questioner is the grammatical speaker of the selected formula; Xuedou supplies the two responses. The turn shows the numerical saying being tested in an interview, not Xuedou newly teaching arithmetic.

In the Shimen teacher's recorded questions and answers, a monk asks about turning a position last night and again this morning, then about both ends turning together. Shimen says this is not the monk's ultimate standard. Asked for that standard he gives late spring approaching summer; pressed on the final matter, he answers nine times nine is eighty-one. Source-named Shimen Huiche voices the selected answer, which terminates this sequence of demands rather than explaining an esoteric calculation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 州曰：『九九八十一。』『挂角後如何？』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB453.xml). Yuanjie Jingying raises Yunju's comparison of a hunting dog losing all trace when an antelope hangs by its horns. Yunju twice answers six times six is thirty-six; after hearing this, Zhaozhou says his elder brother is still there and twice answers the corresponding questions with nine times nine is eighty-one. Yuanjie then criticizes one as stuck on a high peak and the other as unable to emerge from the sea, assigning blows to both. Zhaozhou owns the quoted formula; Yuanjie owns this present appraisal, and Yunju is the compared earlier teacher.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且祇解戰賊，不能殺賊。忽有人問歸宗：家賊難防時如何？劈脊便棒。何故？豈不見道：齊之以禮，上堂，舉：百丈和尚示眾云：汝開田了，我與汝說大義。僧云：開田了，請和尚說大義。丈展兩手，白雲端和尚拈云：百丈說大義祇於此，當時再參馬祖底向什麼處去也？若言更有在，未免與蛇𦘕足。且道：作麼生得知百丈老人立地處？乃云：客來無茶點，蒿湯備禮儀。師云：白雲要見百丈再參馬祖底道理，直是好笑，笑須三十年。又道：作麼生得知百丈立地處，也與笑三十年？客來無茶點，蒿湯備禮儀，也與笑三十年？三笑而九十年，為復笑白雲批判未當？為復別有道理？汝諸人若撿點得出，歸宗拄杖子兩手分付；苟或未然，幾度醉歸明月夜，笙歌引入𦘕堂前。上堂，舉溈山問雲巖云：承聞子在藥山，是否？巖云：是。溈云：藥山大人相作麼生？巖云：涅槃後有。山云：如何是涅槃後有？巖云：水洒不著。雲巖却問：未審百丈大人相作麼生？山云：巍巍堂堂，煒煒煌煌。聲前非聲，色後非色。蚊子上鐵牛，無你下觜處。師云：二尊宿說大人相，何異指鹿為馬？忽有人問歸宗：虎丘大人相作麼生？祗對佗道：九九百百，半青半白。上堂，舉：睦州示眾云：裂開也在我，揑聚也在我。有僧問云：如何是裂開？州云：三九二十七，菩提涅槃，真如解脫，即心即佛。我且與麼道，你又作麼生？僧云：某甲不與麼道。州云：盞子落地，楪子成七片。雲峰悅，云：相罵饒你接觜，相唾饒你潑水。師云：我且問你諸人：雲峰恁麼拈提，為復是見睦州意耶？明睦州語耶？歸宗因行，不妨掉臂。不是禪，不是道，不是玄，不是妙。久立，伏惟珍重。上堂，僧問：藥山小參不點燈，德山小參不答話，未審意旨如何？師云：二俱瞎漢。僧云：可謂端居坐底人，意氣衝斗牛。師云：不是這箇道理。僧云：恩深轉無語，懷抱自分明。師云：切忌錯承當。僧又問：崇壽和尚道：識得橙子，周匝有餘。未審和尚還肯佗也無？師云：老僧深肯佗。僧云：雲門道：識得橙子，天地懸殊。又作麼生？師云：穿却鼻孔。僧云：澤廣藏山，理能伏豹。又作麼生？師云：君子懷義。僧云：還許學人露箇消息也無？師云：有何不可？僧云：犀因翫月紋生角，象被雷驚花入牙。師云：猶帶文彩在。僧禮拜，師乃云：識得橙子，周匝有餘；識得橙子，天地懸殊。若向周匝有餘處會

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 且祇解戰賊，不能殺賊。忽有人問歸宗：家賊難防時如何？劈脊便棒。何故？豈不見道：齊之以禮，上堂，舉：百丈和尚示眾云：汝開田了，我與汝說大義。僧云：開田了，請和尚說大義。丈展兩手，白雲端和尚拈云：百丈說大義祇於此，當時再參馬祖底向什麼處去也？若言更有在，未免與蛇𦘕足。且道：作麼生得知百丈老人立地處？乃云：客來無茶點，蒿湯備禮儀。師云：白雲要見百丈再參馬祖底道理，直是好笑，笑須三十年。又道：作麼生得知百丈立地處，也與笑三十年？客來無茶點，蒿湯備禮儀，也與笑三十年？三笑而九十年，為復笑白雲批判未當？為復別有道理？汝諸人若撿點得出，歸宗拄杖子兩手分付；苟或未然，幾度醉歸明月夜，笙歌引入𦘕堂前。上堂，舉溈山問雲巖云：承聞子在藥山，是否？巖云：是。溈云：藥山大人相作麼生？巖云：涅槃後有。山云：如何是涅槃後有？巖云：水洒不著。雲巖却問：未審百丈大人相作麼生？山云：巍巍堂堂，煒煒煌煌。聲前非聲，色後非色。蚊子上鐵牛，無你下觜處。師云：二尊宿說大人相，何異指鹿為馬？忽有人問歸宗：虎丘大人相作麼生？祗對佗道：九九百百，半青半白。上堂，舉：睦州示眾云：裂開也在我，揑聚也在我。有僧問云：如何是裂開？州云：三九二十七，菩提涅槃，真如解脫，即心即佛。我且與麼道，你又作麼生？僧云：某甲不與麼道。州云：盞子落地，楪子成七片。雲峰悅，云：相罵饒你接觜，相唾饒你潑水。師云：我且問你諸人：雲峰恁麼拈提，為復是見睦州意耶？明睦州語耶？歸宗因行，不妨掉臂。不是禪，不是道，不是玄，不是妙。久立，伏惟珍重。上堂，僧問：藥山小參不點燈，德山小參不答話，未審意旨如何？師云：二俱瞎漢。僧云：可謂端居坐底人，意氣衝斗牛。師云：不是這箇道理。僧云：恩深轉無語，懷抱自分明。師云：切忌錯承當。僧又問：崇壽和尚道：識得橙子，周匝有餘。未審和尚還肯佗也無？師云：老僧深肯佗。僧云：雲門道：識得橙子，天地懸殊。又作麼生？師云：穿却鼻孔。僧云：澤廣藏山，理能伏豹。又作麼生？師云：君子懷義。僧云：還許學人露箇消息也無？師云：有何不可？僧云：犀因翫月紋生角，象被雷驚花入牙。師云：猶帶文彩在。僧禮拜，師乃云：識得橙子，周匝有餘；識得橙子，天地懸殊。若向周匝有餘處會

Senses.Explanation: Jiufeng's fieldwork image for shared work with Yangqi when Yangqi is invited to lead a monastery. After Yangqi is invited to an abbacy, Jiufeng stops him and welcomes him as a fellow practitioner. Yangqi asks what their shared practice is; Jiufeng says one pulls the plow and the other drags the harrow. Yangqi tests the claim of equality by asking who goes first, and Jiufeng hesitates. Eryin Mi retells the exchange with a verse, Miaoyun considers how Jiufeng might have answered, and Longxiang treats the two masters' exchange as a joint performance. The farm tools mark cooperative work, while Yangqi's question exposes a possible division of rank.

At a separate winter-solstice hall talk, Gulin Qingmao marks the turning of extreme yin toward yang while the cold wind still blows. ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 為甚如此？嚴曰：只為春行冬令。天井新云：得人一牛，還人一馬。理固然矣。檢點將來，也是死而不弔。法忍謐云：溈山杖子，千里同風。者僧送到，對面千里。且道誵訛在甚麼處？甜瓜徹蒂甜，苦匏連根苦。天目律云：香嚴與麼，也是珊瑚枕上兩行淚，半是思君半恨君。東塔熹云：溈山送杖，養子之緣。香嚴便哭。不為分外則且置，祇如道春行冬令又作麼生？報恩須是報恩人。風穴喜云：者僧為溈山送拄杖，兵隨印轉；香嚴接得便哭，將逐符行。且道春行冬令意旨如何？咄！退菴智云：大小香嚴把不住，被拄杖子轉不得。者僧一拶，幾乎屈辱大溈。宗門拈古彚集卷第二十一宗門拈古彚集卷第二十二古杭白巖嗣祖沙門淨符彚集△南四杭州徑山洪諲禪師杭州徑山洪諲禪師因僧問：奄息如灰時如何？諲曰：猶是時人功幹。曰：幹後如何？諲曰：耕人田不種。曰：畢竟如何？諲曰：禾熟不登場。天童華云：鳳閣香沉，雪巢夜冷，半窓明月，和氣靄然。正與麼時，且道歸宗與徑山還有相見分也無？見與不見且止，只如這僧與麼還具眼麼？苟或未然，雲藏無縫襖，鳥宿未萌枝。保寧茂云：打鼓弄琵琶，相逢兩會家。九年人不識，幾度過流沙。滁州定山神英禪師滁州定山神英禪師因󳬰樹省行脚時參問：不落數量，請師道。山提起數珠曰：是落不落？曰：圓珠三竅，時人知有，請師圓前話。山便打，樹拂袖便出。山曰：三十年後搥胸大哭去在。樹住後示眾曰：老僧三十年前被定山熱瞞一上，不同小小。雪竇顯云：定山用即用，爭奈險；󳬰樹知即知，要且未具。擇法眼試請辨看。古南門云：眾中商量道：󳬰樹被定山瞞。殊不知定山被󳬰樹引得牽筋動骨，諸人還辨得麼？如辨不得，莫待三十年，只今也須搥胸大哭一上。且道古南又具什麼眼？襄州延慶法端禪師襄州延慶法端禪師因僧問：蚯蚓斬為兩段，兩頭俱動，佛性在阿那一頭？慶展兩手。洞山价別云：即今問底在阿那一頭？笑巖寶別云：但呼闍黎。僧若應諾，却問云：端的在阿那一頭？慧雲盛別。慶和聲便打云：在這一頭。京兆米和尚京兆米和尚問僧：近離甚處？曰：藥山。米曰：藥山老子近日如何？曰：大似一片頑石。米曰：得漝麼鄭重。曰：也無你提掇處。米曰：非但藥山米，胡亦漝麼。僧近前顧視而立。米曰：看！看！頑石動也。僧便出。雪竇顯云：米胡也縱奪可觀，爭奈死而不弔。溈山

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 。三十年後，覓一个舉話底也難得。下座。進退兩班，上堂。楊岐輔慈明，三十年風行草偃；仰山夢說法，五百眾膽顫魂驚。年來世殊事異，名存實亡，無本可據。澹湖者裏不比諸方，非公言直道不萌于心，非截鐵斬釘不施其用。當進退行藏之際，是全機出沒之時，道箇如龍如虎、如鳳如麟，早是相埋沒了也。良久，召侍者，云：三十年後不得忘却者話。下座。上堂，舉：僧問雲門：如何是雲門一曲？門云：臘月二十五。師云：會得雲門一曲，便會臘月二十五；會得臘月二十五，便會雲門一曲。有底道：臘月二十五便是雲門一曲。錯了也。僧又問：唱者如何？且緩緩，依稀越國，彷彿揚州。上堂：新年頭有佛法，也瞞你諸人不得。新年頭無佛法，也瞞你諸人不得。因甚如此？日日是好日。請都寺，上堂。拈却漏燈盞，放出自己光明；踏碎破砂盆，突出衲僧巴鼻。颺下從前活計，斬新舊日規模。同心同德，翊贊藂林；利己利人，荷檐佛祖。所以道：化育之本，物我同途；離相離名，古今不易。正與麼時，出格一句作麼生道？驚羣須是英靈漢，敵勝還它獅子兒。上堂，舉雪竇和尚云：春力不到處，枯樹亦開花。九年人不識，幾度過流沙。師云：日不待火而熱，月不待風而凉。雖然，志士苦日短，愁人知夜長。謝覺非、鄧山長上堂，舉郭功甫請東山演和尚陞座，於法座前燒香云：此一瓣香爇向鑪中，為光明雲遍法界供養堂頭禪師，伏願於此雲中方廣座上擘開面門，放出先師形相與諸人描貌。何以如此？白雲巖畔舊相逢，往日今朝事不同，夜靜水寒魚不食，一鑪香散白蓮風。五祖遂云：曩謨薩怛陀鉢怛囉，恁麼恁麼，幾度白雲溪上望，黃梅花向雪中開；不恁麼不恁麼，嫩柳條金線，且要應時來。不見龐居士問馬大師云：不與萬法為侶者是什麼人？大師云：待汝一口吸盡西江水即向汝道。一口吸盡西江水，萬丈深潭窮到底，略彴不是趙州橋，明月清風安可比？師云：大凡是過量人、明過量事，於過量境界中顯過量機、發過量用，直下如平地上險崖、坦夷處孤峻。然美則美矣，其奈五祖老人有打破虗空、回互不犯底手段，所謂動絃別曲，葉落知秋，如珠走盤，不留影跡。山僧與覺非山長三十年吳門交遊之舊，知其出處大節，任重斯道，有古君子之風，又能留心佛祖奧妙之學，至目擊道存處，亦不在楊大年、郭功甫之下。二千里水陸之遙，不易來

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 神會之佛性。六祖打一棒云：者饒舌沙彌，我喚作一物尚不中，何況本源佛性乎？此子設有把茅盖頭，只成箇知解宗徒。此六祖大師迹所不能迹也，更有幾箇老凍膿不能盡舉？下座。上堂，拈主丈云：多不添，水不減，卓主丈，舌是斬身之本。重陽，上堂。不知月之大小，不知歲之餘閏。纔逢此日重陽，又見冬行春令。一九二九，三九二十七，九九八十一。數目甚分明，超過百千億。此時若不究根源，更待當來問彌勒。上堂，舉古者道：上士聞道勤而行之，中士聞道如存若亡，下士聞道而大咲之。師云：澹湖即不然，上士聞道大笑，中士聞道大笑，下士聞道大笑。畢竟如何？到頭霜夜月，任運落前溪。開爐，上堂。火爐頭，無賓主。非即言非，是即言是。丹霞燒木佛，院主眉鬚墮。正是者箇道理。忽有箇漢出來道：是甚麼道理？只向道：舉一隅，不以三隅反，則不復也。上堂。古人道：天寒人寒，大家在者裏。山僧道：天寒人寒，各自歸寮歇去。三界無法，何處求心？四大本空，佛依何住？夜行莫踏白，不是水便是石。下座。冬節，上堂。時復時，日復日，捱到陰極陽生，依舊寒風凜慄。一逕直，二周遮，九年人不識，幾度過流沙。謝秉拂，上堂。一句語具三玄，一玄中具三要。首座也與麼道，藏主也與麼道，只有山僧不與麼道。何也？若與麼道，是汝諸人決定不會三玄三要底道理。豈不見雲門大師云：三乘十二分教，橫說竪說，與我拈針鋒說底道理來看。菩提涅槃，真如解脫，三九二十七，喝一喝，洎錯下注脚。上堂，舉：古人道：言而足，終日言而盡道；言而不足，終日言而盡物。道物之極，言默不足以載；非言非默，議有所極。師云：登山須到頂，入海須到底。黃河三千年一清，蟠桃三千年結實。五祖和尚云：牛角長三寸，兔角長八尺，四溟東海流，般若波羅蜜。下座。為珣首座秉炬。聰明不敵生死，乾慧豈免輪廻？開人天眼目是死句，瞎人天眼目是死句，三世諸佛在火𦦨裏轉大法輪是死句，火𦦨為三世諸佛說法、三世諸佛立地聽是死句。所以道：平地上死人無數，過得荊棘林是好手，火裏迸出青蓮花，水中驚起泥牛吼。元宵，上堂。燈燈相續，物我俱忘，一句無私，當陽顯示。竪起拂子，云：看，看！今佛放光明，助發實相義；古佛與露柱交參，猫兒咬殺老鼠。上堂，拈主丈云：佛佛授手，祖祖相傳，只說者箇，不說那箇

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 九年人不識，幾度過流沙

Senses.Explanation: The nine-year and desert image serves an old-case comment, Gulin Qingmao's two distinct hall occasions, and Daochang Huiyin's answer about Bodhidharma. The sources disagree on who first voiced the line. After the Jingshan Hongyin exchange about a farmer whose grain never reaches the threshing floor, the compilation explicitly assigns the selected couplet to Baoning Mao as a later comment. Its nine years and desert crossings turn the old case toward an unrecognized traveler. A separate Gulin record attributes the same line to Xuedou, so the original authorship remains source-dependent. At a hall talk, Gulin Qingmao explicitly introduces Xuedou as speaker of the inherited verse about a dead tree flowering and nine unrecognized years. Gulin then responds that sun and moon need no fire or wind and contrasts how people experience the length of day and night. This record names Xuedou, whereas the separate X66 compilation assigns the selected couplet to Baoning Mao; the two claims are not harmonized. At a separate winter-solstice hall talk, Gulin Qingmao marks the turning of extreme yin toward yang while the cold wind still blows. He directly voices the selected nine-year and desert line within his seasonal verse, using an old traveler image to punctuate that seasonal reversal. This is a second occasion in the same work, not another work or a copy of his earlier Xuedou quotation. Senses.Explanation: The summer retreat's enclosure, named by its ninety days — the boundary masters draw, keep, strain against, and sometimes dissolve outright. Lan'an Dingxu, at the retreat's start, verses the other side of the rule: ninety days confined, but for one idle beyond things, what confinement, what bond — a silk fan's breeze is enough, let mountains stay green and waters stay blue; Jieshi Zhipeng, closing the retreat, images the rule as netted birds homing to the nest and foxes set to guard tombs, and even three heads and six arms at the spot where birth and death cannot reach, overturning the awakening-hall, is still mooring to a stake; Huanxi Weiyi calls it cutting the crane to lengthen the duck and threading the ox through the horse — two thousand years ago the yellow-faced one drew the boundary on a needle point, and no one has crossed it since; and Xueyan Zuqin holds both horns: east corridor, west corridor, truly not one step moved — yet seated in this hall on this seat, he walks the whole world freely. Xutang Zhiyu, at the night assembly, names the strain: old seals unadorned, new rules in force — ninety days confined is splitting the jar to find the sky, three months protecting life is chopping the zither to stew the crane, leaving the determined nowhere to stretch; Muchen Daomin quotes the ancients' three cages — fish in the net, birds in the cage, the silkworm in its cocoon — then overturns them for his own war-torn, famine-year summer: Tiantong this summer holds no retreat and no confinement; Feiyin Tongrong dissolves the rule into the patch-robed life — roaming free by conditions, what talk of ninety days confined; that is carving ice to seek fire, steaming sand to make rice; and Chaozong Tongren spares no one on either side: at the ninety-day confinement, straining brows and eyes is labor squarely wasted; at the thrice-requested throne-talk, wagging tongues is mutual dulling.

Senses.Note: At the opening of the retreat, the source-named Doushuai Bulin Jian (TEI author Zongjian, absent from the canonical roster) begins his hall talk with the ninety-day and three-month formula, then asks who stands at the doorway. The paired durations frame this retreat opening. At the release from retreat, Cuiya Bi repeats the same duration pair, names binding and unbinding as the monastery rule, and lets the monks go while saying they remain at the same place. The formula marks the retreat’s close. Two independent source settings survive; validation is provisional. At a summer-retreat opening, Tian'an Sheng calls ninety days of confinement and three months' residence the ordinary rule. He contrasts that formula with the energetic monks, officers and workers at Dajue, using it to introduce the present assembly rather than merely repeating a calendar label. On his birthday at the start of the summer retreat, Baichi Xingyuan asks whether the assembly has seen through the original face, Linji's blows, the wild-fox case and Yantou's last word. If so, he says, they need not rely on ninety days confined and three months in residence; the formula becomes a test of what retreat accomplishes.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Amid the ninety-day mirage, the fivefold dharma-body is complete.

Senses.Note: Yunju Yu closes a summer-retreat sermon with this couplet; Yushan Shangsi later quotes it and deliberately changes the practical emphasis for his own retreat audience.

Occurrences.Kwic: 光中有一無位真人，出沒三界，流轉五道，不捨十惡業，不墮五陰身，不除煩惱障，不證涅槃，不憎毀禁，不敬持戒，不經冬，不過夏。汝等諸人還知去處麼？良久，云：九旬陽焰裏，五分法身圓。白雲端禪師結夏云：安居之首，禁足為名。禁足之意，意在進道而護生。衲僧家有何生而可護？何道而可進？唾一唾，唾破釋迦老子面門；行一步，踏斷釋迦老子脊骨。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X64/X64n1260.xml). At the opening of the summer retreat, Yunju Yu describes an unranked person passing through the realms without adopting conventional oppositions, then pauses and gives the nine-decade mirage and complete fivefold dharma-body couplet. Occurrences.Kwic: 文殊。你一念心無差別光，處處總是普賢。你一念心能自在，隨處解脫，此是觀音三昧法。互為主伴，顯即一時顯，隱即一時隱，一即三，三即一，如是解得，方始好看教。夾山善會禪師夾山善會禪師師初在溈山作典座，溈問：今日吃甚菜？師曰：二年同一春。溈曰：好好修事著。師曰：龍宿鳳巢。僧問：從上立祖意教意，和尚為甚麼却言無？師曰：三年不吃飯，目前無飢人。曰：既是無飢人，某甲為甚麼不悟？師曰：祇為悟迷却闍黎。復示偈曰：明明無悟法，悟法却迷人。長舒兩脚睡，無偽亦無真。問：古人布髮掩泥，當為何事？師曰：九烏射盡，一翳猶存。一箭墮地，天下黯黑。僧問：如何是夾山境？師曰：猿抱子歸青嶂裏，鳥銜花落碧巖前。上堂：金烏玉兔，交互爭輝。坐却日頭，天下黑暗。上唇與下唇，從來不相識。明明向君道，莫令眼顧著。何也？日月未足為明，天地未足為大。空中不運斤，巧匠不遺蹤。見性不留佛，悟道不存師。尋常老僧道：目覩瞿曇，猶如黃葉。一大藏教是老僧坐具，祖師玄旨是破草鞋。寧可赤脚，不著最好。上堂：不知天曉，悟不由師。龍門躍鱗，不墮漁人之手。但意不寄私緣，舌不親玄旨。正好知音，此名俱生話。若向玄旨疑去，賺殺闍黎。困魚止濼，鈍
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X68/X68n1319.xml). Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings. In Jiashan Shanhui's recorded encounter, a monk asks why an ancient practitioner spread his hair over muddy ground. ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 三軍。陳如尊者一坐坐斷，四百箇衲僧上無攀仰、下絕己躬，常光現前，壁立萬仞。拈拄杖，云：有利無利，不離行市。今年桃李貴，一顆直千金。上堂：無邊身菩薩不見如來頂相，才說無邊便有限量，爭見如來頂相？如來頂相只在諸人面前，巍巍堂堂，離一切見。解夏，上堂：長期百二十日，短期九十日。無繩自縛底有甚數？十字縱橫底有甚數？上堂：諸佛不著便，諸祖不著便。今日老僧不著便，你諸人上來也不著便。顯掌財下火，要與你顯露本有靈光。你三度為掌財來，情塵濃厚，紅爐𦦨上雪花飛。上堂：真人面前，一點伎倆用不得。九烏射盡，一翳猶存。一箭墮地，天下不黑。上堂：諸上座體取佛意，無事安樂底，便是一得永得。不同善財暫時斂念，樓閣門開。上堂。性非垢淨，湛然圓滿。諸佛菩提，眾生煩惱。驀拈拄杖擊香臺，云：針眼魚吞却嘉州大像。上堂：明暗色空，不曾礙人。一念周沙界，日用萬般通。湛然常寂寂，常轉自家風。園頭下火。園中種作不違時，是汝為頭都得知。莫謂荼毗沒分付，老僧不見一莖眉。上堂：明上座悟去，六祖與他道：什麼不思善，不思惡？正當恁麼時，那箇是明上座本來面目？若因此，老僧今日亦恁麼舉，諸人何不悟去？明上座禮拜，問曰：上來密

Entries.SourceTerm: 九萬里鵬從海出，一千年鶴遠天歸

Senses.PreferredTarget: A roc rises from the sea across ninety thousand li; a thousand-year crane returns from the distant sky.
SearchAliases: A roc rises from the sea across ninety thousand li; a thousand-year crane returns from the distant sky.
Senses.Note: Foyin Liaoyuan gives the couplet as an answer to a monk, while Qingyuan Yuzhe Zhi independently uses it to close a layman's bathing celebration.

Occurrences.Kwic: 耶？將謂白日射人眼花，暗室光纔自見，一經雪地剝落，始能享其四時耶？謾落商量，閒疑且置，只要是箇削鐵斬釘漢子，定然拔俗，不肯因循。即今發願初心，原在拄天拄地，無我備我本來尊貴，不用雲門訝為希奇，多生一笑，自盡今時，早已攪長河為酥酪。今日平田居士全身拶入青原，作箇白髮嬰兒，供養索訶世界，換骨脫胎，忍俊真奇，三界忘言，已周七步，盡古今是一大浴盆，誰不手舞足蹈？又何待即心即佛、非心非佛作指頭餳？又何待嚼乾矢橛、綑麻三斤為麻胡嚇哉？且喜大眾各沾一杓，共飽一頓，又道箇甚麼句子酬他慶快聻？九萬里鵬從海出，一千年鶴遠天歸。」下座。戊申元旦，洪浪淵請上堂。師云：「向上一句，釋迦未曾投胎；末後一句，彌勒只堪捧腹；中間一句，空累文殊、普賢。兩眼兩腳爭差，尚且惹人擯出。青原今日即不然，三世諸佛、百千祖師一齊按過，滿口道不得底，峰頭海眼噴雪；盡力舉不起底，閒居閣裏拏雲。只為矜茫錯過，太無事生，所以盤錯相逢，又從頭起。」拂拂，云：「此話且置，秪如洪崖浪起，跳出西山二十夏，剩此眉毛三千里，不忘磬眼，故鄉本色，笑出上風特地臘底，逆流恰值百年中半。以此元旦作第一齋，淨居雲版生大歡喜，又道箇甚的好聻？但願春風齊
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB313.xml). At a hall talk for layman Pingtian's bathing celebration, Qingyuan Yuzhe Zhi depicts him as a white-haired newborn and the world as a bathing basin. He closes with a roc rising from the sea and a long-lived crane returning from the sky. The couplet is Qingyuan's own celebratory response.

Occurrences.Kwic: 用同時。忽然不拈不放。你向甚麼處卜度。直饒會得倜儻分明。若遇臨濟德山。便須腦門著地。且道伊有甚麼長處。良久曰。曾經大海休誇水。除却須彌不是山。廣因要禪師廣因要禪師上堂：古者道，祇恐為僧心不了，為僧心了總輸僧。且如何是諸上座了底心？良久曰：漁翁睡重深潭濶，白鳥不飛舟自橫。雲居了元佛印禪師雲居了元佛印禪師僧問：如何是佛？師曰：木頭雕不就。曰：恁麼則皆是虗妄也。師曰：梵音深遠，令人樂聞。○問：如何是諸佛說不到底法？師曰：蟻子解尋腥處走，蒼蠅偏向臭邊飛。曰：學人未曉，請師再指。師曰：九萬里鵬從海出，一千年鶴遠天歸。○問，大修行人還入地獄也無。師曰，在裏許。曰，大作業人還上天堂也無。師曰，鰕跳不出斗。曰，恁麼則鑊湯爐炭吹教滅，劒樹刀山喝使摧。師曰，自作自受。乃曰，適來禪客出眾禮拜，各以無量珍寶布施大眾。又於面門上放大光明，照耀乾坤，令諸人普得相見。於此明得，可謂十方諸佛各坐其前，常為勞生演說大法，豈假山僧重重註破。如或未然，不免橫身狥物。乃橫按拄杖曰，萬般草木根苗異，一得春風便放花。○師一日與學徒入室次，適東坡居士到面前，師曰：此間無坐榻，居士來此作甚麼？士曰：暫借佛印四大為坐榻。師曰

Entries.SourceTerm: 九萬里鵬纔展翅，一千年鶴便翱翔

Senses.PreferredTarget: The roc has only just spread its wings for ninety thousand li; the thousand-year crane is already soaring.
SearchAliases: roc spreads wings, thousand-year crane soars
Senses.Note: The three sources are distinct present capping sermons. They do not prove who first composed the poetic couplet, and the cited old masters in the surrounding sermons are not its local speakers.

Occurrences.Kwic: 以來，幸喜大眾安享九十日。今之告圓，曾不聞有一人半箇妄自見神見鬼，箇箇眉毛依舊在眼上。然雖如是，且古風穴道祖師心印狀似銕牛之機，去即印住，住即印破，秪如不去不住，印即是？不印即是？九萬里鵬纔展翅，一千年鶴便翱翔。」下座。禹州若愚禪人同大心領眾為師慶誕，請上堂。「東風御柳撼啼鶯，春意綢繆花物榮，聲色堆頭親透脫，見聞知覺了無生。所以道：欲識佛性義，當觀時節因緣，時節若至，其理自彰。且作麼生是佛性義？莫是㘞地一聲時喚作佛性義得麼？莫
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB203.xml). At a Lantern Festival sermon closing the winter retreat, Yun'e Xi celebrates the assembly's ninety days without fanciful visions, then raises Fengxue's old image of the ancestral mind seal as an iron ox. He asks what it means neither to go nor to stay, and answers with the line of the roc spreading its wings and the thousand-year crane soaring. Yun'e voices the couplet as his present cap and leaves the seat; Fengxue supplies the earlier problem, not these closing words.

Occurrences.Kwic: 之恩、能難能之事。運臨濟金剛王寶劍，喝下全彰；用德山山行拄杖，覿面分付。是則全是、見則全見，不落凡聖階梯，直下徹空已見，致使佛魔勦絕、凡聖兩忘。且道正眼流通如何展演？」良久，云：「九萬里鵬纔展翅，一千年鶴便翱翔。」卓拄杖，下座。上堂。為一如維那付衣拂，云：「昔日大庾提不起，大悲拈出又重新，人天授囑克家種，好掇沙盆震祖燈。」復舉衣示眾云：「這段光彩，自威音那畔佛佛授受、祖祖相傳，今至山僧無敢妄授，須是久經煆煉，鐵額銅頭，不顧危亡
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB288.xml). Asked to display the highest teaching, Hanyu Hongxian strikes questioners with his staff. In the ensuing address he invokes Linji's shout and Deshan's staff as immediate ways of carrying the Chan command, then asks how the true eye continues in circulation. After a pause Hanyu speaks the roc-and-crane couplet, strikes the staff, and descends. The headword is Hanyu's present answer to his own question, not an utterance attributed to Linji or Deshan.

Occurrences.Kwic: 句下。逸格超宗，輝騰今古，在處揭人天正眼，隨方闡微笑宗風。雖是恁麼人，方說恁麼話；欲行恁麼事，須是恁麼人。雖然，猶是功勳邊事，只如獨超物外一句又作麼生道？」驀拈拄杖，卓一卓，云：「九萬里鵬纔展翅，一千年鶴便翱翔。」小參小參小參。「欲明向上關頭，須奮逸格超群之志，方可了生脫死，紹續宗乘。近來學者斷不以生死為念，只圖延緩過期，者裏經冬、那邊度夏，將別人殘羹剩飯亂噇亂嚼，竟不知裏面是何滋味，卻道：那個堂頭好機鋒，那個堂頭好偈頌。如斯
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB434.xml). At a summer-retreat release sermon, Fazhuang Zhiyuan says that holding fast for ninety days and opening a narrow passage both serve the teaching. He asks what phrase could exceed even accomplished work. Fazhuang raises his staff, strikes it, and delivers the roc-and-crane couplet as his cap. The image functions as the answer to that live challenge rather than a biographical report about either bird.

Senses.Explanation: The great roc and long-lived crane supply an expansive closing image when a teacher presses for a response beyond a limited formulation of the matter. Yun'e Xi ends a release-from-retreat sermon by asking what lies beyond Fengxue's iron-ox image of the ancestral mind seal, then voices the roc-and-crane couplet and leaves the seat. Hanyu Hongxian has just answered questioners with a staff blow and has described Linji's shout and Deshan's staff as the living command; when he asks how the right eye is carried forward, he answers with the same couplet and strikes his staff. Fazhuang Zhiyuan, releasing a summer retreat, distinguishes holding fast and opening a way, asks for a line that goes beyond merit-making, and caps it by raising and striking his staff with the roc and crane. All three are current Tier 2 capping speeches by the resident teachers, each in a different sermon.

SearchAliases: The great peng has barely spread its ninety-thousand-mile wings; the ancient crane already soars
Senses.Note: The paired birds image names an opening movement too vast to measure by ordinary progress. It is an image of awakened scope, not a claim about actual birds.

Occurrences.Kwic: 自熱。今日四月初一，孟夏稍熱，且道是何物？若也識得，天地日月、森羅萬象無纖毫過患；脫或未然，來年更有新條在，惱亂春風卒未休。」下座。佛誕上堂。「今朝正是四月八，釋梵王宮生悉達，秪為時人不知因，年年枉遭惡水潑。眾中若有知因者，出來為這老漢雪屈。」良久，云：「若無，雲門大師來也。」拽拄杖下座，一時打散。上堂，舉：「僧問雲門：『如何是透法身句？』門云：『北斗裡藏身。』大慧云：『雲門恁麼道，只答得法身句，未答得透法身句。今日或有人問徑山：「如何是透法身句？」向他道：「蟭螟眼裡放夜市，大蟲舌上打鞦韆。」』」師云：「通玄今日又且不然，如有問如何是透法身句，劈脊便棒，縱使不會，管教永劫不忘。」下座。久雨將晴，施主臨行請上堂。「春雲欲開未開，春雨欲息未息，日頭欲出未出，行人欲歇未歇。為甚如此？只因途路不得力。忽然雲開日出，便是到家時節。」豎拂云：「還見麼？若也見得徹去，管教當下心息。」擲拂子，下座。上堂。「通玄峰頂好個消息，若人識得，參學事畢。」喝一喝，云：「不煩久立。」便下座。受嘉興金粟山請落板，同眾赴上堂。「懸起也，杲日當空；放下也，孤明歷歷；不懸不放，諸佛莫知，鬼神莫測。且符到奉行一句作麼生道？九萬里鵬纔展翼，百千年鶴便翱翔。」下座。師到會稽曹山護生庵，眾請上堂。「適來未陞座時已為諸人相見了，而今陞座重為諸人起模畫樣，便乃散去，猶較些子。更待老僧鼓兩片皮、掉三寸舌，為之說法，向句裡思量、言中取則，正是業識茫茫無本可據。」驀拈拄杖架肩云：「楖栗橫擔不顧人，直入千峰萬峰去。」便下座。密雲禪師語錄卷第一終密雲禪師語錄卷第二嗣法門人法藏編浙江嘉興金粟山廣慧禪寺語錄浙江嘉興金粟山廣慧禪寺語錄天啟四年，檀越蔡聯璧請，於五月六日入院，至山門，云：「佛語心為宗，無門為法門。新長老打破牢關，一任擎頭帶角。」舉杖云：「還見麼？」佛殿，云：「釋迦已過去，彌勒猶未來，正當恁麼時，法柄在阿誰手裡？」乃展坐具云：「遍覆三千及大千。」土地堂，云：「伽藍神，叢林主，一瓣香，兩手舉。」便燒。祖師堂，云：「西天四七、東土二三，盡在這裡默默地商量個事，今日一時捉敗，且道以何為驗？」插香云：「以此為驗。」眾請上堂，師指法座云：「須彌燈王如來已為諸人露頭露面了也，還見麼？若也未然，更須撥轉上頭行。」遂陞座拈香云：「此瓣香端為祝延今上聖壽，恭願萬邦歸聖化，八表偃干戈。」次拈香云：「此瓣香奉為滿朝文武、合國官僚、本山護法、遠近檀那，同明般若正因，共證

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉：「雪巖遠祖云：『海水不可斗量，虛空不可尺度，淨地不可撒沙，爛泥不可著腳。』不肖兒孫又且不然，海水可以斗量，虛空可以尺度，淨地可以撒沙，爛泥可以著腳。且道與古人是同？是別？」遂拍手，云：「摘楊花，摘楊花。」康熙丙午九月廿一日，師受安龍鎮王檀越請，住玉泉禪院。拈帖云：「香爐匙筯總是家裏底事，擲之三千里外又且何妨？然雖如是，也須知事宣過始得。」入院。云：「無意道人之意，無門解脫之門，無意又無門，且從甚麼處入？渾身在裏許。」便進。佛殿。云：「似真像假，似假像真，合眼禮你三拜，不免換卻元辰。」便拜。伽藍。云：「護法不如護己，護己則無一法。珍重！珍重！」據室。云：「諸佛列祖到者裏也須卷舌，且道利害在甚麼處？」拈拄杖一齊打散。上堂。拈香祝聖罷，次拈云：「此一瓣香，自從蹋破草鞋，一旦親蒙印可，此是第五回拈出，供養成都府昭覺丈雪大和尚，用酬法乳之恩。」斂衣敷坐。白椎竟，問：「昨日蘭溪，今朝玉泉，如何是地頭底事？」師云：「退後著。」進云：「不解隨人腳跟轉。」師便打，乃云：「道無異徑，理絕殊途，言是則無一不是，言非則無一不非，者裏是非俱剷、理事圓融，直得如天普蓋、似地普擎。正恁麼時，且報恩一句作麼生道？九萬里鵬纔展翼，百千年鶴便翱翔。」防禦王公送衣帽至，上堂。「頂新帽，穿新衣，著新鞋，子細思量，秖是令人不該。」遂顧視左右，云：「且道為甚如此？」起身合掌，云：「難消。」結制，上堂。「祖令當行，人天喪膽，有不惜性命者麼？」顯首座問：「最初威音王，末後樓至佛，樓至即不問，未審威音王參見甚麼人？」師便打，座一喝，師云：「你道是那一箇？」座又喝，師連打兩棒，座拂袖歸眾。問：「未見和尚前，和尚在學人肚裏；已見和尚後，和尚在學人當面。肚裏底是？當面底是？」師云：「還我性命來。」士無語，師連打兩棒。問：「如何是玉泉境？」師云：「萬壽山宜天地準。」「如何是境中人？」師云：「眼見耳聞。」僧禮拜，師便打，乃云：「大道沒影蹤，非結亦非解，答定腳頭直教徹，此中大有好光彩。」又云：「今朝十月十五，會集人天共語，不容分外提持，秖許腳跟薦取，推倒真如法界，掃蕩諸佛列祖。直須心心相照，則無一事不合天地；念念相依，則無一理不貫古今。茲承王檀越開此無遮勝會，請山僧陞座，向人天眾前唱無說之說、演不言之言，山僧秖得厚著臉皮，說幾句澹話以酬所請。汝等諸人參須真參、悟須實悟，庶不虛今日相聚。珍重。」薦嚴，上堂。「日日日東出，日日日西沒，細細躊躕太反覆，不如洗

Occurrences.Kwic: ？凡歟？」卓拄杖，一喝，云：「分明記取。」解制，陞座。僧問：「衝開碧浪即不問，放出神鼇事若何？」師云：「腳下波生。」進云：「覓火和煙得，為甚玅高峰七日不相見？」師云：「到即不點。」僧作禮，云：「今日親見和尚。」師云：「要你知休。」迺云：「揭起虛空蓋一層，收來放去任縱橫。草鞋似虎威獰甚，拄杖如龍活潑生。踏倒玄關須轉步，驀行鳥道貴抽身。諸方若遇談玄者，切莫遭他鬼眼睛。眾兄弟！一期既畢，銀山鐵壁撞得破否？猛虎金鈴汝解得否？驪龍玄珠汝摘得否？若得相應，不妨東去西去，盡大地總是汝毘盧真境。稍涉廉纖，正好按下雲頭，向冷湫湫地去，思箇思不得的、覓箇覓不得的。思不得的作麼思？鐵網拋空，神龍透海。覓不得的作麼覓？夜半篩鑼，賊身忽露。恁麼舉揚，還解交得麼？」遂擊拂，云：「能知減灶添兵處，終不和身困馬陵。」下座。攖寧禪師住黎川羅漢禪寺語錄卷之二門人德因編侍者德玹記錄住黎川羅漢禪寺師受蘇州府吳江縣黎里鎮縉紳、工部金，同太史張、刑部韋、鴻臚朱，文學毛、秦、沈、周、吳，眾檀信并法侶剖初、元超等請入院。師指山門，云：「玄珠斲象，拈來掣古揮今；亞目豁機，到此越終超始。龍象交參，秪如入門一句作麼生道？」震聲一喝，云：「九萬里鵬纔展翼，百千年鶴便翱翔。」彌勒殿。「笑破機微，頓絕背向。今日相逢，原無異樣。是則固是，擔荷雖繇此老，卷舒還在渠儂。」韋馱殿。舉香，云：「護法護人全憑這著，這著圓通無處不豁，直教魔外不能窺，果是獅兒堪蹴踏。」大殿基。「碧落青霄，未是道人活計。墻壁瓦礫，豈宜吐舌弄唇？畢竟如何折合？」顧左右，云：「大家扶起空王殿，百億須彌側耳聽。」毘盧佛殿。「坐斷毘盧，方堪話會；踏翻玄奧，始解抽機。到此為甚重添註腳？」展具，云：「因我得禮汝，自倒還自起。」即拜。伽藍殿。拈香，云：「一紙不曾饒，全憑驗作手。親受靈山囑，提持豁諸有。觸音法法盡包羅，萬古叢林好善護。」祖師殿。舉香，云：「燒穿鼻孔，摵斷莖眉，殃及兒孫，一番話墮。燈燈無盡響孤峰，海底飛塵漫別弄。」方丈。「握肘後靈符，剪狐狼狂見。挽已墜之風，擊寒爐發焰。正令當行，未歸早驗。」遂據座，云：「道合君臣猶未貴，深登堂奧始容參。」是日，眾請上堂。師指法座，云：「觸破人天正眼，擊開無孔鐵錘，迥露當央，萬機點首。」卓拄杖，云：「且看山僧話墮去也。」遂陞座，拈香祝聖畢，次拈香云：「此一瓣香，惡惡辣辣，孤峭難親，啐啄不呼玄要，針芥頓絕暗明，捉敗紫霞峰頂，頓然觸發毒聲，秪得今日對眾拈出，爇向

Occurrences.Kwic: 處？」復卓拄杖云：「萬派皆歸海，千山盡仰宗。某本粥飯常行，山林朽櫟，道既慚於先哲，德復媿于時賢，是以四載以來雖領名藍，常居學地，只知栽田博飯，竟忘豎拂拈椎。茲承法姪慧公屈臨虔請、同門世弟著力成褫，勤舊兩序之同誠、檀越諸山之合德，自知業緣既就，迴避無門，推出人天眾前，只得將錯就錯，掇上曲彔床上，隨例撒土撒沙。適纔世楷大師互相出手舉保壽因緣，山僧一時應機便恁麼荅，可謂不逢楊意，誰知司馬之長？既遇鍾郎，寧惜高山之韻？雖然，若作與麼商量，未免瞎卻天下人眼；不作與麼商量，亦未免瞎卻天下人眼。畢竟如何？真金自有真金價，別寶還他碧眼胡。」復白椎云：「諦觀法王法，法王法如是。」請維那、書記、藏主、知客、侍者上堂。問：「量才補職即不問，定國安邦事若何？」師云：「肐膊不外曲。」進云：「定國安邦即且置，量才補職作麼生？」師云：「打鼓弄琵琶。」進云：「恁麼則秖奉一人天地貴，從他諸道自分權。」師云：「出群須是英靈漢。」僧禮拜。師乃云：「黃龍躍出死水，立三關而驗人；一字不著畫，香林錯污紙衣。毛錐未舉以前，文彩已全彰；白椎時絕對待，聲光直透威音外。一代教，缽羅娘，隨色摩尼耀八荒，主賓互換，敲唱鏗鏘。」喝一喝，云：「九萬里鵬纔展翼，百千年鶴便翱翔。」請世楷大師為座元，上堂。「普化成褫臨濟，建立黃檗宗旨，譎而不正；懶安佐助溈山，發明百丈家風，比而不周。若要楷模一世、法式千秋，成佛祖嘉謨、作人天眼目，須是沒量大人孤危不立、曲屈垂慈，提綱挈領處無黨無偏、橫身為物時無彼無我，內舉不遺戚、外舉不避仇，自然表率得人、紀綱得所，皇皇穆穆、躋躋蹌蹌，激揚向上宗猷、成就不思議事，何心不契？何法不周？苟不如然，直饒文殊、普賢交光相羅，未免即聾從昧；觀音、彌勒合掌擎拳，不出與頑用囂。成得什麼邊事？還委悉麼？更聽一偈：獨掌從來不浪鳴，互相出手有同聲；青蛇脫匣雲雷吼，艸偃風行令正行。」開爐，上堂。「爐鞴靈通，鈍銕一烹成大器；鉗鎚妙密，精金百煉轉光新。固是讓諸方好手以天地為爐、陰陽為炭，熬清風、炙明月，未免徒張施設。神鼎隨分尺八五分掘箇地爐，凡來一切諸餘，無論銕額銅頭、凡情聖解，悉向此中冰消瓦解，說什麼金裹頭、銀裹腳、藥汞禪、木刻鷂？任是金剛圈、栗棘蓬、陝府銕牛、嘉州大象，直教毫末不存，單單只有箇華陽洞口石烏龜不曾動著。何故？留取諸人九十日內證他成鱉。」華嚴菴怡谷靜主請上堂。展拂子云：「大眾見麼？一處透脫，千處萬處光輝；一機洞明，千機萬機圓轉。此座不離華

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 處？」復卓拄杖云：「萬派皆歸海，千山盡仰宗。某本粥飯常行，山林朽櫟，道既慚於先哲，德復媿于時賢，是以四載以來雖領名藍，常居學地，只知栽田博飯，竟忘豎拂拈椎。茲承法姪慧公屈臨虔請、同門世弟著力成褫，勤舊兩序之同誠、檀越諸山之合德，自知業緣既就，迴避無門，推出人天眾前，只得將錯就錯，掇上曲彔床上，隨例撒土撒沙。適纔世楷大師互相出手舉保壽因緣，山僧一時應機便恁麼荅，可謂不逢楊意，誰知司馬之長？既遇鍾郎，寧惜高山之韻？雖然，若作與麼商量，未免瞎卻天下人眼；不作與麼商量，亦未免瞎卻天下人眼。畢竟如何？真金自有真金價，別寶還他碧眼胡。」復白椎云：「諦觀法王法，法王法如是。」請維那、書記、藏主、知客、侍者上堂。問：「量才補職即不問，定國安邦事若何？」師云：「肐膊不外曲。」進云：「定國安邦即且置，量才補職作麼生？」師云：「打鼓弄琵琶。」進云：「恁麼則秖奉一人天地貴，從他諸道自分權。」師云：「出群須是英靈漢。」僧禮拜。師乃云：「黃龍躍出死水，立三關而驗人；一字不著畫，香林錯污紙衣。毛錐未舉以前，文彩已全彰；白椎時絕對待，聲光直透威音外。一代教，缽羅娘，隨色摩尼耀八荒，主賓互換，敲唱鏗鏘。」喝一喝，云：「九萬里鵬纔展翼，百千年鶴便翱翔。」請世楷大師為座元，上堂。「普化成褫臨濟，建立黃檗宗旨，譎而不正；懶安佐助溈山，發明百丈家風，比而不周。若要楷模一世、法式千秋，成佛祖嘉謨、作人天眼目，須是沒量大人孤危不立、曲屈垂慈，提綱挈領處無黨無偏、橫身為物時無彼無我，內舉不遺戚、外舉不避仇，自然表率得人、紀綱得所，皇皇穆穆、躋躋蹌蹌，激揚向上宗猷、成就不思議事，何心不契？何法不周？苟不如然，直饒文殊、普賢交光相羅，未免即聾從昧；觀音、彌勒合掌擎拳，不出與頑用囂。成得什麼邊事？還委悉麼？更聽一偈：獨掌從來不浪鳴，互相出手有同聲；青蛇脫匣雲雷吼，艸偃風行令正行。」開爐，上堂。「爐鞴靈通，鈍銕一烹成大器；鉗鎚妙密，精金百煉轉光新。固是讓諸方好手以天地為爐、陰陽為炭，熬清風、炙明月，未免徒張施設。神鼎隨分尺八五分掘箇地爐，凡來一切諸餘，無論銕額銅頭、凡情聖解，悉向此中冰消瓦解，說什麼金裹頭、銀裹腳、藥汞禪、木刻鷂？任是金剛圈、栗棘蓬、陝府銕牛、嘉州大象，直教毫末不存，單單只有箇華陽洞口石烏龜不曾動著。何故？留取諸人九十日內證他成鱉。」華嚴菴怡谷靜主請上堂。展拂子云：「大眾見麼？一處透脫，千處萬處光輝；一機洞明，千機萬機圓轉。此座不離華

Occurrences.Kwic: 知，知是妄覺、不知是無記。到者裏，三世諸佛只可自知、六代祖師全提不起、一大藏教詮註不及，直饒與麼，衲僧門下正是就地彈󳭋，有甚麼共語處？豈不見首山和尚云：我若坐時你須立，你若坐時我須立，坐則共你坐、立則共你立，箇事如隔窓看馬騎，擬議即沒交涉。大眾還會麼？拈得便用、把得便撲，一句定綱宗，青天飛雪雹。卓主丈，下座。上堂：如來非智巧，智者必以如來為宗；祖師非妙得，得者必以祖師為旨。宗旨既定，清濁自分。一句全提，當陽顯示。聞無聞而聞盡，見無見而見忘。重重鐵壁銀山，處處通天活路。所以道：九霄絕翳，何用穿通？一道神光，未甞昏昧。正與麼時如何？萬緣脫去輕浮世，一性常來看落花。劉總領入山齋僧，上堂，舉：朱行軍一日入寺齋僧，行䞋次，有云：直下是，直下是？一僧云：直下是箇甚麼？行軍便喝，僧云：幸是佛法中人，惡發作麼？行軍云：喚作惡發得麼？僧便喝，行軍云：鉤在不疑之地。師云：朱行軍廣陳供養，功不浪施，者僧不肯承當，遂成虗設。應菴和尚云：行軍拈出倚天長劒，者僧披襟敢衝雪刃。雖然兩不相傷，爭奈二俱弄險？與麼說話，曲為當時。忽若劉總領今日堂中行䞋，道箇直下是，直下是，是汝諸人作麼生酬對？若也道

Occurrences.Kwic: 。於此不堅確精進，成辨道業，他日何面目見父母師友乎？然此事不在多知多解，只要據實而論。大眾會麼？舉不顧，即差互，坐斷上頭關，截斷千差路，更不著商量，千聖齊却步。喝一喝，下座。中夏普說：心不附物，意不停玄，大智非名，真空絕迹。是汝諸人十二時中向甚處措足？直下無事，墮在見聞覺知，纔涉安排，未免依草附木。兄弟！據實而論，盡十方世界有甚麼物與汝為緣？為對三乘十二分教？達磨西來，直指人心，見性成佛，增一絲毫不得。及至颺向他方世界，無依無欲，離相離名，無去無來，不生不滅，也減一絲毫不得。九霄絕翳，何用穿通？一道神光，未甞昏昧。所以恁麼也得，不恁麼也得，恁麼不恁麼總得。如王寶劒，孰敢當鋒？擬欲擡眸，橫屍萬里。古人垂一機，示一境，至痛快為人處，直是透頂透底，情生智隔，想變體殊。情未生時，隔箇甚麼？此亦是一期方便控你入處，為你未曾及到者箇田地。所以有佛有法，有玄有妙，有向上向下，者邊那邊自作障礙，曠大劫來不得自由。況此事豈是你赤肉團上心識搏量底事？心若無事，萬法不生，意絕玄微，纖塵何立？雲門云：直得觸目無滯，達得名身句身，一切法空，山河大地是名，名亦不可得，喚作三昧。性海俱備，猶是
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1412.xml). In a midsummer general talk, Gulin Qingmao asks where listeners can set their feet when mind clings to nothing. He directly speaks the cloudless-sky and unclouded-light couplet, then says both affirmation and denial can work. The line supports his challenge to stop manufacturing barriers.

Occurrences.Kwic: 地、日月星辰、卉木叢林、人畜草芥悉皆是法，阿那箇是境？於此見得倜儻分明，便可向高高峰頂橫行、深深海底闊步。莫有恁麼俊快衲僧？試出來𮞏相唱和。僧問：達磨未來時如何？答云：塞壑填溝。進云：來後如何？答云：輝天鑑地。進云：畢竟如何？答云：須彌山，香水海。乃云：豁開戶牖，萬里不挂片雲；當軒者誰？突出青天白日。恁麼，恁麼，南瞻部洲打鼓，北󳬂單越升堂；不恁麼，不恁麼，海底輥紅塵，山頭飛白浪；恁麼中，不恁麼，十字街頭吹銕笛，千峰頂上放憨癡；不恁麼中，却恁麼，三更夜半唱巴歌，無端驚起梵王睡。九霄絕翳，何用穿通？一道神光，未甞昏昧。拈拄杖，云：看！看！上方拄杖子變作釋迦老子，放大光明，照徹三千大千世界，上窮有頂，下透金輪，於其中間演說摩訶大般若，無二無二分，無別無斷故，直得毗盧遮那如來化成妙寶樓閣，多寶世尊涌出七層妙塔，交相贊賀云：善哉！善哉！希有！希有！正恁麼時，東海龍王忍俊不禁，踊躍歡喜，鼓吉祥風，澍甘露雨，却向靈山會上報諸大眾道：群陰既剝，一陽已生，󳫴運推移，日南長至，應時納祜，慶無不宜，廓萬古之徽献，混一團之和氣。卓拄杖一下，云：水歸大海波濤壯，雲到蒼梧氣象高。復舉：洞山冬

He then lifts his staff and tells the assembly to look, describing it as radiating light and teaching wisdom. The line prepares that present staff display.

Senses.PreferredTarget: “filial devotion is called the precepts”
AlternateTargets: filial devotion is named as the precepts
SearchAliases: filial devotion is named as the precepts
Senses.Explanation: “Filial devotion is called the precepts” is wording explicitly quoted from the Brahma’s Net Sutra, not an anonymous Chan maxim. Yongjue Yuanxian contrasts filiality in the Buddha teaching with the Confucian duties he lists: material support, reverence, establishing one’s reputation, burial, and sacrifice; he then locates filiality in recognizing that the child's dharma-body is the parents' original body rather than stopping at those services. Zhuanyu Heng quotes the same scripture while arguing that filial devotion and keeping the precepts are not two commitments. Shiyu Mingfang directly applies the clause in a memorial address. In Hanyue Fazang’s record, an unnamed questioner raises the scriptural wording and Hanyue answers it. These Chan uses quote, explain, apply, or test one scriptural clause.
Senses.Note: The preferred target retains quotation marks because the headword is repeatedly presented as wording from the Brahma’s Net Sutra.

Occurrences.Kwic: 至我釋門梵網一經，演說菩薩大戒，開口便道孝名為戒，亦云孝順至道之法，是儒釋竝以孝為首重也。

Occurrences.Kwic: 復謂禪人曰：「子孝行心切？持戒心切？」曰：「孝行、持戒俱切。」曰：「何為二心俱切？」曰：「父母必要孝，戒行必要持。」病僧曰：「子將孝與戒為兩橛耶？豈不聞《梵網經》云：『孝名為戒。』是則孝外無戒，戒外無孝。

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：「如何是釋迦如來口放戒光？」師云：「風為掃地使，月作點燈娥。」進云：「如何是孝名為戒？」師云：「灶裏生青草，鍋中叫碧蛙。」進云：「如何是亦名制止？」師云：「忍餓長盤腳，開齋過別峰。」

Occurrences.Kwic: 說話竈婦乳兒皆能言之。若曰佛身。不亦遠矣。然普現羣生前隨緣靡不周。且置之勿論。又指何物為菩提座耶。或謂佛身充滿此座亦充滿。無二無二分無別無斷故。若曰菩提座上別有佛身。則不可得為恒處也。然既充滿。且無常生死有漏世間。又向甚麼處安著。或者引永嘉謂夢裏明明有六趣覺後空空無大千。既覺矣。謂佛身謂菩提座。亦無地可寄。又何言說而非寐語哉。學者未能真誠夢覺。雖曰讚佛乃謗佛耳。宜審諸宜審諸。盡十方世界是清淨法身當體。如千日並照。了無纖毫障蔽。無端為一點無明當面覆却。以故仰而觀之之謂天。俯而視之之謂地。廣而窺之之謂法界。以至山高水深晝明夜暗風動塵起雲騰鳥飛。與夫披剝萬象剖析精明。欲覔所謂法身則空然無有也。由是引起分別。堅執妄情喚空作色不得。指明為暗不得。視親作踈不得。轉憎為愛不得。要識無明面目麼。只這箇轉不得底不欠一毫。忽有箇強主張者道。我但見空不作空。見色不作色。惟以一清淨法身觀之。是亦是矣。奈何謂空謂色之見卒未能忘。又作清淨法身之能觀所觀初未曾冺須知只箇未忘未冺底。政是根本無明。直下絞瀝不乾洗滌未淨。若欲頭頭上明物物上顯。誠不啻隔靴抓癢也。如圓覺謂。此無明者非實有體。如夢中人夢時非無及至於醒了無所得。與麼說來。無明豈有實體定性可得。乃全體是清淨法

Senses.Explanation: Yunmen’s last question in a three-disability test turns a monk’s claimed inability back on him. In the inherited test, a monk asks Yunmen how to meet people who cannot see, hear, or speak. Yunmen has the monk bow, step back, come forward, and answer whether he understands; when the monk says he does not, Yunmen asks whether he is not mute. Lingshu Yuan quotes the sequence and sets his own verse after a later critique of it. Caotang Nüyun Shi also retells the case, then says the monk understood only Yunmen and Xuansha’s Chan, before giving a challenge about his own. Wujian Xiandu quotes Yunmen’s question and tests the medical image anew, saying Yunmen’s medicine could kill but not bring life. The old question is one voice and the current appraisals differ.

Senses.Explanation: The Buddha rebukes an outsider who presses him to choose whether all things are permanent or impermanent; later teachers test his silence and answer. An outsider asks the World-Honored One whether all things are permanent and then whether they are impermanent. He does not answer either question. When the outsider demands why an all-knowing teacher stays silent, the Buddha says that all these questions are idle speculation. Shipuzhi presents the encounter in an old-case verse sequence and adds a poem on the power of the refusal. Liaozong Chaojian cites it and asks his listeners to hear the force of the Buddha's silence. Gaofeng Yuanmiao offers a separate critique, warning that even explaining the silence can add more speculation.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 殺修禪定者，譬如有人自塞其耳，高聲太呌，求人不聞。此等名為欲隱彌露。清淨比丘於岐路行，不踏生草，況以手拔，云何大悲？取諸眾生血肉充食，名為釋子。又道：若不斷偷修禪定者，譬如有人水灌漏巵，欲求其滿，縱經塵劫，終無平復。若諸比丘衣鉢之餘，分寸不畜，乞食餘分，施餓眾生。又道：若諸世界六道眾生，雖則身心無殺盜婬，三行已圓，若大妄語，則三摩地不得清淨。如刻人糞為旃檀形，欲求香氣，無有是處。婬殺盜妄既已消亡，戒定慧學自然清淨。若太虗之雲散，如大海之波澄。得到這般田地了，方可以參禪，方可以學道。你且道禪又作麼生參？道又作麼生學？從上以來，多有樣子。福源不惜口嘴，略舉數段。二祖初到少林，參禮達磨，斷臂立雪，悲泣求法。達磨曰：諸佛最初求道，為法忘形。汝今斷臂，求亦可在。二祖曰：諸佛法印，可得聞乎？達磨曰：諸佛法印，匪從人得。二祖曰：我心未安，乞師安心。達磨曰：將心來，為汝安。二祖曰：覔心了不可得。達磨曰：我為汝安心竟。二祖於此悟入。這箇便是為法忘軀，參禪學道第一樣子。大梅常禪師參問馬祖：如何是佛？祖曰：即心是佛。常領旨，直入大梅山卓菴。後馬祖聞之，令僧去問曰：和尚見箇甚麼道理便住此山？常曰：馬祖向我道即心是佛，我向這裏住。僧曰：馬祖佛法如今又別了也。常曰：作麼生別？僧曰：如今又道非心非佛。常曰：這老漢惑亂人未有了日在，任他非心非佛，我只管即心即佛。其僧回舉似祖，祖曰：梅子熟也。這箇便是有決定信，無疑惑心，參禪學道第二箇樣子。臨濟初在黃蘗會下行業，純一首座問曰：上座在此多少時也？濟曰：三年。首座曰

Entries.SourceTerm: 汝但究理，坐看三二十年

Senses.PreferredTarget: Simply investigate the principle; sit and see for twenty or thirty years.
SearchAliases: simply investigate the principle; sit and see for twenty or thirty years.
Senses.Note: The duration expresses persistence, not a guaranteed timetable or permission for mere inert sitting. Later comments distinguish sustained inquiry from waiting for a future experience.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：金佛不度爐，木佛不度火，泥佛不度水，真佛內裏坐。菩提涅槃，真如佛性，盡是貼體衣服，亦名煩惱。實際理地，甚麼處著？一心不生，萬法無咎。汝但究理，坐看三二十年。若不會，截取老僧頭去。夢幻空華，徒勞把捉。心若不異，萬法一如。既不從外得，更拘執作麼？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X64/X64n1260.xml). Outline Record of the Successive Patriarchs. Zhaozhou Congshen tells the assembly that gold, wooden and clay Buddhas cannot survive furnace, fire and water, and calls exalted religious terms close-fitting garments that can themselves become afflictions. After saying that when one mind does not arise the many things are without fault, he urges them to investigate the principle and sit and see for twenty or thirty years; if they still do not understand, they may cut off his head. He immediately warns against grasping dreamlike appearances and seeking outside oneself. The headword commits his instruction to prolonged actual investigation, with his own head as the emphatic pledge. It does not say that the passage of years alone produces understanding.

Occurrences.Kwic: 趙州云：汝但究理，坐看三二十年。若不會，截取老僧頭去。評：趙州著甚死急！然雖如是，歲月長，討箇三二十年不異心者也難得。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X63/X63n1257.xml). Boshan’s Chan Admonitions. Boshan, Wuyi Yuanlai, quotes Zhaozhou's instruction together with the offer of his head, then asks why Zhaozhou is in such desperate haste. Yet, he adds, the years are long, and someone whose resolve does not alter for twenty or thirty years is hard to find. His preceding comment on Zhaozhou's unmixed application of mind says this is not failure to use the mind but keeping it from being mixed; his following comment directs investigation beneath one's own robe. Zhaozhou remains the quoted speaker. Boshan's teasing question and acknowledgment of the difficulty make the pair an occasion to examine steady resolve, rather than a simple promise attached to a number of years.

Occurrences.Kwic: 示眾。諸上座！一月過一月，一日過一日，作麼生用心？須要徹首徹尾。你看古人在者裏坐破七箇蒲團，是何等用心？今人發脚參方便想。秉拂開堂。趙州道：汝但究理，坐看三二十年。若不會，截取老僧頭去。佛法無多子，久長難得人。山僧三十年前在博山見苦心參究底人尚多，如今絕不見用心。者一種用心，只是將心待悟，此病入了膏肓，畢生不治。大眾！切須老實做去。無論三二十年，就使一生不徹，亦如此做去。但存一副乾淨肚腸，有何相為不得？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1443.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zongbao Daodu. Kongyin Daodu asks the assembly how they apply themselves as months and days pass, contrasting an ancient teacher who wore through seven cushions with people already imagining that they will open a teaching hall as soon as they begin traveling. He quotes Zhaozhou's twenty-or-thirty-year instruction and pledge, then says the teaching is not complicated but people who persist are rare. Recalling earnest investigators at Boshan thirty years earlier, he criticizes the present habit of waiting for awakening as a disease beyond cure. He urges honest practice even if one never penetrates it in a lifetime. The pair is therefore actively turned against both haste for public authority and passive expectation; the apparent tension between long effort and waiting is made explicit, not smoothed away.

Senses.Explanation: Four teachers turn a question about location back on the person asking. In a J37 winter-solstice hall, a monk asks what person is untouched by the movement of days and seasons. The teacher asks where he is right now and refuses the monk further praise. At another J37 departure hall, a monk presses whether the original mind is concealed anywhere; the teacher asks where he is right now, and the monk bows. The teacher calls that bow mistaken and explains why in his final address. A J39 teacher retells a scholar asking Changsha where a thousand buddhas live. He says he would answer the same question with “Where are you right now?” and follow another query with a blow. In an X72 meal-offering hall, a monk asks about the Buddha station. The teacher answers with the same question; when the monk says he is here, the teacher calls him an ordinary being. Four different scenes use immediate location as a counterquestion.

Senses.Note: In the old encounter, Mazu looks toward a whisk and Baizhang asks whether to use it or leave it. Mazu asks how Baizhang will teach when he opens his lips later; Baizhang lifts and replaces the whisk, and Mazu shouts. Feiyin, Yinyuan, Baichi, Jie'an, and Yushan give separate current verses or comments on this question and its outcome. The exact words are Mazu's inside the old case, not the later record owners' own question.

Senses.Explanation: Three different teachers ask the same short question in three separate encounters. In a sermon about balancing seated practice and work, the Xueguan teacher cites an older exchange: Qingyuan Xingsi sees Shitou sitting and asks what he is doing there. Shitou says that he is doing nothing, then resists Qingyuan’s suggestion that this is merely idle sitting. Xueguan uses the exchange to tell his present community that neither sitting nor work should be held one-sidedly. In Xiangyan’s preface to a set of ox-herding pictures, another old encounter supplies the exact question. Mazu Daoyi asks Shigong what he is doing; Shigong answers that he is herding an ox and describes pulling it back by the nose when it strays into grass. Xiangyan uses the episode to introduce the pictures and their instructional setting. The Anheidou collection preserves a third scene: while the young Dongming Xubai Huican is cutting radishes, his teacher Tanran asks what he is doing. Huican replies literally that he is cutting radishes, then turns the exchange into a challenge about killing and yielding. The exact words remain ordinary, but each source gives them a distinct addressee and purpose.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB300.xml). In a different dialogue, Chaozong answers a monk who treats Mazu's final shout as the sole great function. He lists the cake, nose-twisting, mounting and descending the seat, glance at the whisk and the selected teaching question as equally great responsive acts. Senses.Explanation: Mazu turns Baizhang's question about using the whisk into a test of his future ability to teach. The reply is followed by raising and replacing the whisk and Mazu's shout; later commentators examine whether those acts reveal full responsiveness or attachment to an established understanding. Chaozong Tongren compares the case with political consolidation under Qin and Han and with Gaofeng's later training under Xueyan. Mazu's question draws Baizhang's prior understanding into view; replacing the whisk still clings to the root, while the shout cuts off the remaining hope of possession. The historical analogy makes this a sustained present account of unfinished differentiation and its removal, rather than a second telling claimed as independent history. In a different dialogue, Chaozong answers a monk who treats Mazu's final shout as the sole great function. He lists the cake, nose-twisting, mounting and descending the seat, glance at the whisk and the selected teaching question as equally great responsive acts. Distinguishing the teacher's functioning from the student's realization, he drives the questioner out with his staff. This live explication gives the selected question a role different from the earlier political analogy. Foyuan Chegang quotes Baizhang's renewed visit, the selected question, the whisk raised and replaced, and the shout that leaves Baizhang deaf for three days. His own verse follows the irreversible force of the spoken word and the paired using-or-leaving question with willow fluff drifting east and west, then drains Dongting Lake and asks where fish and dragons can lodge. The verse appraises the case's movement beyond a settled place; it is not Mazu's continuing speech. Wanfeng Tongzhen Zhishan quotes the whisk case together with Huangbo's later refusal to inherit Mazu merely through hearing about his great function. His verses connect finding the way home with establishing a household and contrast bodily sight with hearing, while warning against merely dreaming of protruded tongues and deaf ears. Senses.PreferredTarget: Since you are so, I am so too
SearchAliases: since you are so, i am so too
Senses.Note: Huineng answers a student, “Since you are so, I am so too,” after an exchange about realization that is not stained. Tianyin uses it to insist that words follow years of inquiry rather than replace them. Feiyin reads Huairang’s answer as refusing a fixed thing to describe. Lanshi draws the same formula into another encounter with Qingyuan. Qianyan calls it a ready-made stamp and asks whether descendants have stopped at the phrase. The equality in the reply asks to be recognized, not imitated.

Senses.Explanation: The Buddha's instruction turns Ananda's request for an ancient ritual back to the bowl he is already carrying. In the inherited exchange, the Buddha sends Ananda into town with his alms bowl, tells him to follow the rite of the seven past awakened ones, then responds to Ananda's request to identify that rite by calling his name and sending him off with the bowl again. Feiyin Tongrong raises this exchange while speaking to monks whose own alms-bowl journey was interrupted by soldiers and officials; he calls the bowl's duty weighty. Sanfeng Zang quotes the same exchange and follows it with a verse on an ordinary moment of seeing and hearing. Xiuyelin also raises the case, then warns that the Buddha is caught within Ananda's frame and asks whether anyone can get out. These are separate later readings of one inherited dialogue, rather than three new occasions when the Buddha spoke the command.

Senses.Note: In the larger scripture pair, the Buddha's finger press makes the sea seal shine, while a momentary stirring of mind raises dusty entanglements. Yingshan, Miyun, Shiqi, and Jingting quote the line before answering or questioning it. Shuijianhai uses the contrast in his own current address; Yunwai and Chushi quote it, then apply it to their assemblies. The line warns about grasping movement of thought, not the mere fact that awareness appears.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 溽暑中手到病除，鮮有不驗。雖然，更有一種病、一味藥，猶未識在。且道是甚麼病？甚麼藥？要識病麼？古人云：「我有一病，非世所醫。」又，馬大師一日院主問云：「近日尊候如何？」師云：「日面佛、月面佛。」者是。要識藥麼？昔日文殊命善財採藥曰：「是藥者採將來。」善財遍觀大地，無不是藥，卻來白云：「無有不是藥者。」文殊曰：「是藥者採將來。」善財遂於地上拈一莖草度與文殊，文殊接得，呈示眾曰：「此藥亦能殺人，亦能活人。」試問初引：曾識得非世所醫的病麼？還識得日面佛、月面佛的落處麼？并識得文殊示眾，能殺人亦能活人的藥麼？忽然看徹，直教通身是病、通身是藥，信手拈來，要用便用，那時殺也在你、活也在你，灑灑落落，利己利人，無施不可。經云：「諸供養中，法供養最。」不然，自己一場熱病到來，要且如何下手？所謂業茫茫，無本可據。至囑，至囑。示自如禪人示自如禪人上人既號自如，有何不如，更要山僧開示？若要山僧開示，則自如不自如了也。釋迦老子云：「如我按指，海印發光。汝暫舉心，塵勞先起。」《金剛經》云：「應如是住，如是降伏其心。」夫既如是，則上人分上不少一法、不多一法，既不見多一法、又不見少一法，則上人全體自如，豈待山僧問示？雖然，也須親證到者個田地始得。古人云：「參禪一著了要敵生死，不是說了便休。」昔僧問趙州和尚：「萬法歸一，一歸何處？」州云：「我在青州做領布衫，重七觔。」上人作麼生會？如不會，直須豎起脊梁，剔起眉毛，咬定牙關，仔細看他是個什麼道理？看來看去，一朝忽然看徹，則全是上人自受用三昧。個裏覓些子，如也不可得、是也不可得，不如也不可得、不是也不可得，如是、不如是總不可得，不可得亦不可得。如是向者裏翻個身來，便喚作如亦得、是亦得，不如亦得、不是亦得，如是喚作不如是亦得、不如是喚作如是亦得，乃至一切皆得，者便是真自如也。然雖如是，上人莫見山僧如是說便作如是之見。示吳道人示吳道人尊翁敬溪居士來云：「道人因病，痛念生死。倘到無著落處，沒個把柄，如何是好？」要與山僧討個把柄，分明指示個著落處。山僧別無指示，即此沒把柄便是把柄、無著落處正好著落。不見古人云：「我宗無語句，亦無一法與人。」道人若信得及，直下擔當，莫容擬議，不見有聖、不見有凡，不見有生滅、不見有去來，乃至一切是非、人我等相俱不可得。如是，則世間

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 亦乃為鄉人也，安得不互相發明末後大事？觀指汝精勤持誦為最上乘歟？淨守毗尼為最上乘歟？乃至造像刻經、飯僧修供為最上乘歟？若最上乘者，生不知來處，死不知去處，實人生至大之事。今既撒手，宜當體悉。」舉火炬曰：「觀指本來面目，覿體靈光，我今為汝真實指點，終不虛也。」為了然煆骨。「盤走珠兮珠走盤，信手拈來顆顆圓，非獨汝今能證了，十方諸佛體皆然。體皆然，體皆然，火燄光中生白蓮。」為王吏科起棺。「富貴功名當等閒，難留生死片時間。兒嬌室內腸幾折，父老堂中淚欲潸。四十一年真作夢，百千萬劫返家山。而今琴劍誠無用，望斷秋風人不還。雖然，一色杏華紅十里，狀元歸去馬如飛。」下壙。「到家田地不多爭，七尺深深埋白雲。莫謂今朝空手去，文章千古一匡墳。」為亡僧舉火。「生前多為別人忙，死後枯形實可傷，一副皮囊值甚物？煙消火滅看郎當。雖然，山僧更為點出金剛不壞身，令汝往來自在。」舉火炬，曰：「箇裏無私全正令，衲僧鼻孔好流通。」為五臺菴指印封缸。「如我按指，海印發光。汝暫舉心，塵勞先起。只如指禪，建五臺梵剎於八省通衢之地，開古林戒壇於衰殘落莫之秋，是塵勞先起耶？海印發光耶？今日總歸瓦棺內，任從佛眼覷無門。」為尼大智舉火。「般若大智如大火聚，近之則通身燎卻，豈容立地而思？智禪智禪知不知？曇華一朵插頭時。」為慧鎧慈念入塔。「六角亭內，無縫塔中，安身穩便，受用何窮？慧鎧卸兮干戈靜，慈念息兮睡正濃，春山萬里雙眸碧，華鳥一聲塔戶封。」為念真入塔。「一念純真，未是到家消息；吳山越水，任爾腳下遊行。蹋破芒鞋歸去後，玲瓏塔裏好安身。」為憨石珂禪師舉火。「蘇州有底真州賣，拓出滿盤不吝生，今日盡情都撒下，一天雪月釣舟橫。雖然，老僧為汝轉末後法輪去也。」遂擲火炬。為宗一舉火。「腰包頂笠南詢久，果未成時華未開，回首可憐無限意，桂華包裏坐蓮臺。宗禪宗禪胡為哉？此際不須多指示，火光堆裏絕塵埃。」入塔。「九日登高，諸方舊例；重陽入塔，金粟新條。黃華滿目兮，無窮富貴；西風透體兮，不盡風流。湘北潭南休更覓，家山穩坐樂悠悠。」為雲澤侍者舉火。「麟角鳳毛世所艱，銀墻鐵壁腳頭寬，歸根落葉頂𩕳句，一吸神鼇滄海乾。」攛火炬，曰：「從教遍地起波瀾。」為禹峰禪師舉火。「破家散宅走西東，覓得驪珠皮袋中，三載挂瓢胥浦上，一朝脫化向秋空。生緣自謂蘇州有，宗派

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 闍梨近離什麼處？山云：湖南。哲云：觀察使姓什麼？山云：不得他姓。哲云：名什麼？山云：不委他名。哲云：還治事否？山云：自有廊幕在。哲云：還出入否？山云：不出入。哲云：豈不出入？洞山拂袖便行。明日，哲入僧堂，云：昨日對二闍梨一轉語不稔，今請二闍梨道：若道得，開粥相待過夏。速道！速道！山云：太尊貴生。師云：要會尊貴麼？報恩不開。這兩片皮，諸人向什麼處摸索？上堂：秋風涼，秋夜長，天河無起浪，月桂不聞香。耳到聲邊聲到耳，從教露草泣寒螿。中秋，上堂。舉：雲巖掃地次，道吾云：何得太區區生？巖云：須知有不區區者。吾云：與麼則第二月也。巖豎起帚，云：這箇是第幾月？吾拂袖出去。雲門云：奴見婢殷勤。師云：雲巖豎起帚，道吾便出去，總是第二月，那箇是不區區者？此夜一輪滿，清光何處無？探元帥回，上堂。兵隨印轉，紀信登九龍之輦；將逐符行，霍光賣假銀之城。然則有符必有將，有印必有兵。兵在這裏，印在什麼處？良久，云：報恩今日，小出大遇。上堂。如我按指，海印發光；汝暫舉心，塵勞先起。師云：我不似黃面老人打破狼藉，喚什麼作海印？將那箇為塵勞？覔針鋒許了不可得。諸山至，上堂。僧問：如何是在窟師子？師云：頭頂天。進云：如何是出窟師子？師云：脚踏地。進云：如何哮吼師子？師云：還聞麼？進云：即今聞也作麼生？師云：伏唯尚享。乃云：一花開，大地春；一葉落，天下秋。動絃別曲貴知音，瞬目揚眉早蹉過。然則不犯之令，把斷要津；無味之談，塞斷人口。德山棒，臨濟喝，俱胝豎指，魯祖面壁，歸宗斬蛇，大隋燒畬，石鞏張弓，子湖看狗，或則平田淺草，或則鐵壁銀山，或則掣電轟雷，或則和泥合水，全提正印，獨振宏綱，檢點將來，不無滲漏。所以即心即佛，今時未入玄微；非心非佛，猶是指蹤之極。向上一路，千聖不傳，學者勞形，如猿捉影。還有趣向分也無？平蕪盡處是青山，行人更在青山外。復舉：僧問黃龍璣和尚云：禪以何為義？璣云：以謗為義。師云：若有人問南湖：禪以何為義？向他道：以贊為義。且道謗的是？贊的是？眼見則瞎，耳聽則聾，口說則啞，心思則窮，天際雪埋千丈石，洞門凍折數株松。初冬回寺，上堂。僧問：昔日有僧問大隋：劫火洞然，大千俱壞。未審這箇壞不壞？隋云：壞。僧云：與麼則隨他去也。隋云：隨他去也。此意如何？師云：疑則別參。進云：後來雪竇頌云：劫火光中立問端，

Senses.Explanation: The second half of a scripture contrast warns about a thought that stirs and entanglement that follows. Yingshan, Miyun, Shiqi, and Jingting cite the old saying and test what its contrast means. Shuijianhai voices the pair in a current rite, while Yunwai and Chushi cite it before applying it to present listeners.

Senses.Note: Three distinct current appraisals in J26, J32 and J36 engage one inherited host's utterance. J32 adds Nanming's own verse after the narrative and is not merely passive biography. X79/X80/X81/X84/X85 parallel recensions remain reserve; X66 preserves named substitute comments as a weaker-tier active reserve. The host is the story's Manjushri figure, not the present record's teacher, and Wuzhu is not Asanga.

Occurrences.Kwic: 子之於道也，造次必於是、顛沛必於是。於是而知焉，之為道。上士聞道，勤而行之；中士聞道，若存若亡；下士聞道，大笑之，不笑不足以為道。且道：如何免得笑去？多言數窮，不如守中。」上堂。舉：「無著禪師遊五臺，參禮文殊。至山下，投一寺宿。遇一老翁，祇待次，問曰：『上人從何而來？』著曰：『南方來。』翁曰：『南方佛法如何住持？』著曰：『末法比丘少奉戒律。』翁曰：『多少眾？』著曰：『或三百、或五百。』著問曰：『此間佛法如何住持？』翁曰：『龍蛇混雜，凡聖交參。』著曰：『多少眾？』翁曰：『前三三，後三三。』乃命童子將玻璃盞點茶度著，遂問曰：『南方還有者箇不？』著曰：『無。』翁曰：『尋常將甚麼喫茶？』著無對。時天色已晚，著曰：『擬投一宿，得麼？』翁曰：『汝有執心在，不得宿。』著曰：『某甲無執心。』翁曰：『汝曾受戒不？』著曰：『受戒久矣。』翁曰：『既無執心，何用受戒？』遂命童子送出門外。著見寺無額，問童子曰：『此寺因何無額？』童子指背後金剛，著回首，忽失童子并山寺，只見身在林中。」師云：「文殊熱謾無著，卻乃移華兼蜨至；無著錯過文殊，已曾買石得雲饒。後來明招和尚頌曰：『廓同沙界聖伽藍，滿目文殊接話譚，言下不知開佛眼，回頭只見翠藍山。』要且不識無著。雪竇和尚頌曰：『千峰蟠曲色如藍，誰謂文殊是對譚？卻笑清涼多少眾，前三三與後三三。』要且未見文殊。諸人要見文殊麼？大覺為你頌出：長夏山窗綠正肥，楊華偏愛逐征蹄，關山不盡情難訴，燕子銜將水際飛。然雖如是，要見文殊則易，要識無著則難；要識無著則易，要見大覺則難。何也
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB187.xml). Tian'an Sheng quotes Wuzhu's visit to Wutai, his exchange about southern communities, the glass cup and the request to lodge. The host refuses because Wuzhu still clings; when Wuzhu denies attachment, the host asks why he received precepts. Tian'an then criticizes both Wuzhu and Manjushri, denies that earlier verses fully reach them and gives his own summer landscape verse. He finishes by making recognition of Tian'an himself harder still. The lodging refusal belongs to the old host, distinct from the present appraisal.

Occurrences.Kwic: 頭當枕眠。青州布衫。趙州老，工夫少，布衫做得未恰好。擬將蓋覆天下人，不覺和贓敗露了。急著眼，七觔秤子稱得巧。文喜禪師上五臺，遇一老翁牽牛而行，邀師入寺，呼均提。有童子應聲出迎，翁縱牛引師升堂，堂宇皆耀金色。翁踞床，指繡墩命坐。翁曰：「近自何來？」師曰：「南方。」翁曰：「南方佛法如何住持？」師曰：「末法比丘少奉戒律。」翁曰：「多少眾？」師曰：「或三百，或五百。」師卻問：「此間佛法如何住持？」翁曰：「龍蛇混雜，凡聖同居。」師曰：「多少眾？」翁曰：「前三三，後三三。」翁呼童致茶，并進酥酪。師食之，覺心意開爽。翁提起玻璃盞，問曰：「南方還有這個麼？」師曰：「無。」翁曰：「尋常將甚麼喫茶？」師無對。師睹日晚，遂問：「擬投一宿，得否？」翁曰：「汝有執心在，不得宿。」師曰：「某甲無執心。」翁曰：「汝曾受戒否？」師曰：「受戒久矣。」翁曰：「汝若無執心，何用受戒？」師辭退，翁令童子送。師問童子：「前三三，後三三，是多少？」童召：「大德！」師應諾。童曰：「是多少？」師復問：「此是何處？」童曰：「此金剛窟般若寺也。」師悽然，悟彼翁即文殊也，不可再見。即稽首童子，願乞一言為別。童子說偈曰：「面上無嗔供養具，口裏無嗔吐妙香，心裏無嗔是珍寶，無垢無染是真常。」言訖，均提與寺俱隱。譚玄對面不知名，梵剎重重列錦屏。纔問均提是多少，回頭依舊草青青。陸亙大夫問南泉：「弟子家中有一片石，或時坐，或時臥，如今擬鐫作佛，得否？」泉曰：「得。」陸曰：「莫不得否？」泉曰：「不得。」得與不得，全提片石。倒嶽旋巒，天昏地黑。咄
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J32/J32nB275.xml). Nanming Huiguang recounts the encounter under Wenxi's name. After the lodging refusal and precepts test, the attendant Junti answers the numerical question by calling to him, gives a parting verse and vanishes with the temple. Nanming appends his own verse: discussing profundities face to face without knowing the name, splendid monastic buildings, the question to Junti and green grass after turning back. That verse makes failed recognition its present focus; it does not establish a second historical lodging refusal.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB356.xml). Qiran Chaozhi raises Wuzhu's visit at length, retaining the host's lodging refusal but giving Wuzhu's denial as having no calculating mind. The host answers with the precepts question; later the attendant and temple vanish. Qiran abruptly calls to his own assembly: Wuzhu and Manjushri's faces are here, but what of Junti? He strikes the staff and answers with cool water by a stone and fragrance through flowers. This challenge shifts attention to the attendant and the present audience, beyond merely identifying the old host.

Senses.Explanation: The old host refuses Wuzhu lodging by pointing to attachment, then tests his denial through a question about receiving the precepts. In the inherited Wutai narrative the host is identified as Manjushri, while later teachers scrutinize recognition, failed recognition and the attendant's part in the encounter. Tian'an Sheng quotes Wuzhu's visit to Wutai, his exchange about southern communities, the glass cup and the request to lodge. The host refuses because Wuzhu still clings; when Wuzhu denies attachment, the host asks why he received precepts. Tian'an then criticizes both Wuzhu and Manjushri, denies that earlier verses fully reach them and gives his own summer landscape verse. He finishes by making recognition of Tian'an himself harder still. The lodging refusal belongs to the old host, distinct from the present appraisal. Senses.PreferredTarget: If you want to know Buddha, the one who does not know is it
SearchAliases: if you want to know buddha, the one who does not know is it
Senses.Note: Asked which one is Buddha, Punyayashas replies: if you want to recognize Buddha, the one who does not recognize is it. Asvaghosa presses the difficulty, and their exchange turns to saw and wood. Later masters do more than copy the story. Jie'an follows its opening, Xuzhou turns it into a jewel image, Yingning questions whether the old stump has truly been cut, and Neishao and Zhe'an answer in fresh verses. The line unsettles an easy identification of Buddha.

Senses.Explanation: Sudhana’s reply to Asanga becomes a test of what it means to see Manjushri. In the older exchange Asanga asks Sudhana how he may see Manjushri. Sudhana answers that a single pure thought is enough; when Asanga says he has done so but still sees nothing, Sudhana replies that this is true seeing. Buhui quotes the dialogue during a hall address held for a patron’s family and criticizes both question and answer as failing to work freely. A J37 verse author places the same dialogue among old cases, then answers with a poem about asking directions to a wine shop and wondering who owns the place. Shending Yikui quotes it in a separate case discussion, faults Asanga’s search and Sudhana’s baited hook, and adds a verse on seeing without an object. The three later responses use the same old answer in distinct ways.

Senses.Explanation: Bodhidharma asks his disciples to present their understanding in the old succession account. Baiyu recounts Bodhidharma’s invitation to the disciples, the later response by Huike, and a verse that questions neat divisions into skin and marrow. Zhe’an Fan gives a fuller old succession narrative, with the disciples’ replies and Bodhidharma’s judgments about skin, flesh, bone, and marrow. Hansong Cao quotes the invitation in another lineage verse sequence and follows it with his own critique of the transmission story. The imperative remains Bodhidharma’s older speech; these authors use the lineage account with different degrees of detail and judgment.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Can all of you really trust this?
SearchAliases: can all of you really trust this?
Senses.Note: “Can all of you really trust this?” is a direct challenge to the assembly after a teaching claim. Yunfu asks it after reducing the matter to eating when hungry and sleeping when tired. Yinyuan says the whole world flows from one hair pore and asks for trust. Zhiyan raises his whisk while describing Shakyamuni’s awakening. Faxi says the entire scriptural collection issues from his whisk. Gulin asks whether the present gathering and Buddha land can be accepted as inseparable. Wenmu makes old cases collide in a deliberately startling sequence. Each master asks listeners to test the claim in the moment, not merely agree with a sentence.

Senses.Explanation: A teacher asks the assembled listeners whether they fully understand the teaching just presented. Linye Tongqi turns from an earlier exchange to challenge the assembly, then says that understanding would let them see the point. Dulang addresses the audience after an exhortation about practice and asks the same question before expanding on what such understanding enables. Nouyun Zhenshi asks it after contrasting dramatic teaching devices with his own immediate handling, then gives an image of peaks and streams. Yinxin Foming Jina asks it after saying that his teaching has been set out completely, then answers with winter snow and spring wind. The question is each teacher’s own turn to the audience, not a monk asking for an explanation.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1416.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shuzhong Wuyun. Shuzhong Wuyun quotes Muzhou’s question to his own assembly, compares it with Xuansha’s warning, criticizes both inherited formulations, and sets out his own open-road response with a raised staff.

Senses.Explanation: Muzhou asks his assembly whether they have found a point of entry into the matter he is teaching. Muzhou tells the assembly to find an entry point if they lack one and not to let him down if they have found one. A monk steps forward and promises not to let him down; Muzhou replies that he already has. The X67 collection preserves this complete address and the exchange that tests the claim. In a later hall sermon Shuzhong Wuyun quotes Muzhou’s question alongside Xuansha’s warning, judges the older teachers’ approaches, and points his own assembly toward an open route beyond their formulations. These are the original encounter and one distinct present deployment; other exact copies repeat one of those families.

Senses.Explanation: A teacher turns his address to the whole assembly and asks whether they understand. At an Amitabha assembly Yinyuan Longqi speaks of the western land and this land together, then puts the question to those present. Yun’e Xi asks it after declaring his handling of sayings about mind and Buddha and continues by explaining what recognition would show. Jieweizhou Xingzhou asks it after describing the boundless mind-ground precept teaching associated with the Brahma Net Sutra. Each teacher uses the short question to return the preceding discourse to the listeners.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Do all of you see it?
SearchAliases: do all of you see it?
Senses.Note: “Do all of you see it?” follows an immediate demonstration. Miyun raises a staff but warns that naming the staff as what one sees misses his move. Poshan asks whether a deceased layman has appeared on his staff. Yune gathers two old masters into one gesture. Eryin makes a pool and bridge move against their usual places and asks what is visible. Xiangya raises a staff as Shakyamuni appears; Baishan makes the Buddha appear on his whisk and says both claiming to see and denying sight can deceive. The question tests how the assembly meets the displayed act, not eyesight alone.

Senses.Explanation: The master shows an ordinary object or an impossible scene and asks everyone present whether they see what has just appeared. Miyun, Poshan, and Yune each use a staff to press the question beyond physical sight. Eryin, Xiangya, and Baishan ask after transformed scenery or Shakyamuni appearing in a gesture.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (C/C077/C077n1710.xml). Recorded Sayings of Ancient Venerable Masters. The questioner asks where buddha is during awakening; Huangbo Xiyun’s continuing answer says that the whole world is the questioner’s own self.

Senses.Explanation: Huangbo tells the questioner that mountains, rivers, earth, sun, moon, and stars do not leave the questioner’s own mind: the whole three-thousandfold world is ‘your own self.’ In the Wanling Record, Huangbo Xiyun answers successive questions about deluded thoughts, awakening, and where buddha is found. He says that speech, silence, movement, stillness, sound, and form are all buddha-work, and then gives the headword in his statement that the whole world is the questioner’s own self. The Ancient Venerable Masters recension preserves the same exchange.

Senses.Note: Five distinct engagements are retained: Miyun's supplied action, Zukui Fu's sermon response, Dazhu's explanation, Juefan's interpretation of Caoshan and Dahui's verse. Direct X63 preserves Dazhu's explanation more strongly than its X79/X83/X67 copies, counted once. X83's Caoshan passage explicitly quotes Zhizheng zhuan; expanded discussion identifies Juefan and following verses, so its explanatory voice is not automatically Caoshan or the compilation editor. Two unique appraisals survive here in the same lamp container; their tier remains unchanged. Vimalakirti is the quoted speaker and Subhuti the recipient. No global exhaustion is claimed.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J35/J35nB338.xml). At a hall talk, the nun Zukui Fu raises the same long food challenge and Subhuti's attempt to leave. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X63/X63n1224.xml). In Dazhu Huihai's direct question-and-answer record, a lecturer of the Vimalakirti scripture quotes the difficult food passage and asks for an explanation. Dazhu reads following the six teachers as following the six senses, seeking Buddha outside the mind as an outside path, and the alarming negative clauses as refusing attachment to Buddha, teaching or community. He concludes that such understanding receives the food of joy in the teaching. Vimalakirti remains the speaker inside the lecturer's citation; Dazhu supplies the interpretive answer. The matching lamp copies are not additional families.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不知多知解，翻成壅塞，唯多與兒酥乳，消與不消，都總不知。三乘學道人皆此樣，盡名食不消。食不消者，所謂知解不消，皆為毒藥，盡向生滅邊收，真如之中無此事故。以此知曹山貴正命食，立三墮。又曰：維摩經曰：為壞和合相故，應取食；為不受故，應受彼食。以空聚相，入於聚落，所見色與盲等，所聞聲與響等，所齅香與風等，所食味不分別，受諸觸如智證，知諸法如幻相，無自性無他性，本自不然，今則無滅，此不斷聲色墮所由立也。又曰：須菩提不見佛不聞法，彼外道六師，富蘭那伽葉、末伽黎拘賖黎子、刪闍夜毗羅胝子、阿耆多翅舍欽婆羅、迦羅鳩䭾迦旃延、尼犍陀若提子等，是汝之師，因其出家，彼師所墮，汝亦隨墮，乃可取食，此隨墮之所由立也。又曰：謗諸佛毀於法，不入眾數，終不得滅度，汝若如是，乃可取食，此尊貴墮之所由立也。予甞深觀曹山，其自比六祖無所媿，以其蕩除聖凡之情，有大方便。南泉曰：三世諸佛不知有，狸奴白牯却知有。乃不如曹山止言一墮字耳。覺範三墮頌。類墮頌：紛然作息同，銀椀裏盛雪，若欲異牯牛，與牯牛何別？隨墮頌：有聞皆無聞，有見元無物，若斷聲色求，木偶當成佛。尊貴墮頌：生在帝王家，那復有尊貴，自應著珍御，顧見何驚異？大陽玄曰：此三種須明轉位始得。一曰：水牯牛是類墮，是沙門轉身語，是異類中事，若不曉此意，即有所滯，直是要你一念無私，即有出身之路。二曰：不斷聲色是隨墮，以不明聲色故隨處墮，須向聲色有出身之路。作麼生是聲色外一句？曰：聲不自聲，色不自色。故云不斷指掌，當指何掌也。三曰不受食，是尊貴墮。須是知那邊了，却來這邊行履。

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: ，般若即同無情。翠竹若是法身，翠竹還能應用。座主會麼？曰：不了此意。師曰：若見性人，道是亦得，道不是亦得，隨用而說，不滯是非。若不見性人，說翠竹著翠竹，說黃華著黃華，說法身滯法身，說般若不識般若，所以皆成諍論。志禮謝而去。人問：將心修行，幾時得解脫？師曰：將心修行，喻如滑泥洗垢。般若玄妙，本自無生。大用現前，不論時節。曰：凡夫亦得如此否？師曰：見性者即非凡夫。頓悟上乘超凡越聖。迷人論凡論聖，悟人超越生死涅槃。迷人說事說理，悟人大用無方。迷人求得求證，悟人無得無求。迷人期遠劫證，悟人頓見維摩座主問：經云：彼外道六師等，是汝之師。因其出家，彼師所墮，汝亦隨墮。其施汝者，不名福田；供養汝者，墮三惡道；謗於佛，毀於法，不入眾數，終不得滅度。汝若如是，乃可取食。今請禪師明為解說。師曰：迷徇六根者，號之為六師；心外求佛，名為外道；有物可施，不名福田；生心受供，墮三惡道。汝若能謗於佛者，是不著佛求；毀於法者，是不著法求；不入眾數者，是不著僧求；終不得滅度者，智用現前。若有如是解者，便得法喜禪悅之食。有行者問：有人問佛答佛，問法答法，喚作一字法門，不知是否？師曰：如鸚鵡學人語話，自語不得，為無智慧故。譬如將水洗水，將火燒火，都無義趣。人問：言之與語，為同為異？師曰：一也。謂言成句名語矣。且如靈辯滔滔，譬大川之流水；峻機疊疊，如圓器之傾珠。所以廓萬象，號懸河，剖乎義海，此是語也。言者一字，表心也。內著玄微，外現妙相，萬機撓而不亂，清濁混而常分。齊王猶慙大夫之辭，文殊尚歎淨名之說。今之常人，云何能

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 不知多知解，翻成壅塞，唯多與兒酥乳，消與不消，都總不知。三乘學道人皆此樣，盡名食不消。食不消者，所謂知解不消，皆為毒藥，盡向生滅邊收，真如之中無此事故。以此知曹山貴正命食，立三墮。又曰：維摩經曰：為壞和合相故，應取食；為不受故，應受彼食。以空聚相，入於聚落，所見色與盲等，所聞聲與響等，所齅香與風等，所食味不分別，受諸觸如智證，知諸法如幻相，無自性無他性，本自不然，今則無滅，此不斷聲色墮所由立也。又曰：須菩提不見佛不聞法，彼外道六師，富蘭那伽葉、末伽黎拘賖黎子、刪闍夜毗羅胝子、阿耆多翅舍欽婆羅、迦羅鳩䭾迦旃延、尼犍陀若提子等，是汝之師，因其出家，彼師所墮，汝亦隨墮，乃可取食，此隨墮之所由立也。又曰：謗諸佛毀於法，不入眾數，終不得滅度，汝若如是，乃可取食，此尊貴墮之所由立也。予甞深觀曹山，其自比六祖無所媿，以其蕩除聖凡之情，有大方便。南泉曰：三世諸佛不知有，狸奴白牯却知有。乃不如曹山止言一墮字耳。覺範三墮頌。類墮頌：紛然作息同，銀椀裏盛雪，若欲異牯牛，與牯牛何別？隨墮頌：有聞皆無聞，有見元無物，若斷聲色求，木偶當成佛。尊貴墮頌：生在帝王家，那復有尊貴，自應著珍御，顧見何驚異？大陽玄曰：此三種須明轉位始得。一曰：水牯牛是類墮，是沙門轉身語，是異類中事，若不曉此意，即有所滯，直是要你一念無私，即有出身之路。二曰：不斷聲色是隨墮，以不明聲色故隨處墮，須向聲色有出身之路。作麼生是聲色外一句？曰：聲不自聲，色不自色。故云不斷指掌，當指何掌也。三曰不受食，是尊貴墮。須是知那邊了，却來這邊行履。

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 汝若如是，乃可取食

Senses.Explanation: Vimalakirti ends his unsettling conditions for Subhuti's meal by allowing him to take the food only if he can be thus. Later teachers answer the challenge with proposed departures carrying the bowl, explain its clauses through nonattachment, or connect receiving food with Caoshan's three falls. The conditional is kept within these recorded encounters and interpretations, rather than made into a general rule for accepting alms. In Miyun Yuanwu's supplied replies to old cases, Vimalakirti fills Subhuti's bowl and imposes conditions that reverse his familiar categories of purity, teachers and release, ending with the selected permission to eat. The case says Subhuti is bewildered and puts down the bowl to leave. Miyun supplies the action he would take in Subhuti's place: lift the bowl and dance out. Vimalakirti voices the selected conditional; Miyun's proposed movement is a new answer, not something attributed historically to Subhuti. At a hall talk, the nun Zukui Fu raises the same long food challenge and Subhuti's attempt to leave. She calls his courage small and says she would tell the layman that she can digest such a meal, take the bowl and go. She says this would both stop Vimalakirti's mouth and satisfy body and mind, then challenges anyone wishing to defend him; when nobody answers she points to those with mouths unable to obtain food. The quoted conditional belongs to Vimalakirti; Zukui gives this distinct present response. In Dazhu Huihai's direct question-and-answer record, a lecturer of the Vimalakirti scripture quotes the difficult food passage and asks for an explanation. Dazhu reads following the six teachers as following the six senses, seeking Buddha outside the mind as an outside path, and the alarming negative clauses as refusing attachment to Buddha, teaching or community. He concludes that such understanding receives the food of joy in the teaching. Vimalakirti remains the speaker inside the lecturer's citation; Dazhu supplies the interpretive answer. The matching lamp copies are not additional families. Inside the Caoshan section of the Pointing at the Moon compilation, the expanded text explicitly introduces an excerpt from Zhizheng zhuan after distinguishing Juefan's explanations from Caoshan's own words. That commentator links sensible eating with proper livelihood, then uses successive Vimalakirti passages to explain the origins of Caoshan's three falls. The selected conditional supports the fall from privileged status, and the commentator praises Caoshan for sweeping away ordinary and holy attachments. This is Juefan's source-named interpretive voice, not Caoshan directly delivering all the surrounding prose; the following Juefan verses confirm the local attribution context. Entries.SourceTerm: 汝行與道合，諸佛心即是

Senses.PreferredTarget: When your conduct accords with the Way, this is the mind of the Buddhas
SearchAliases: when your conduct accords with the way, this is the mind of the buddhas
Senses.Note: Futuo Mita asks who is closest if parents are not his true kin and what way is highest if the Buddhas are not his way. Buddhānandi replies that conduct aligned with the Way is the mind of the Buddhas. Chijue and Chaozong use the exchange while speaking of gratitude to parents. Baiyu questions whether the ancestors have really accounted for birth parents. Shixi and Yuansou turn the verse toward years of silence and a student’s return home. This clause connects the old exchange to what a person does, not simply whom one reveres.

Occurrences.Kwic: 虗心，究明自己。自己若明，無一事不是真乘，無一法不為妙用。三界二十五有，八萬四千塵勞，四聖六凡，情與無情，盡向這裏氷消瓦解。當恁麼時，非特報今生父母以德，達今生父母以道。以至歷劫以來，父母無不報之以德，達之以道。豈不見昔日伏駄密多尊者，年五十，口未曾言，足未曾履。且道佗五十年，口不曾言，足不曾履，意在什麼處？一日，見佛陀難提至其家，遽起作禮，而說偈言：父母非我親，誰是最親者？諸佛非我道，誰是最道者？難提以偈答曰：汝言與心親，父母非可比。汝行與道合，諸佛心即是。此便是達親以道，報親以德底張本。只如吾人稟父母之遺體，三年然後免懷抱，如何說箇父母非我親底道理？吾人剃除鬚髮，著佛衣，喫佛飯，依佛而住，當行佛行，作麼生說箇諸佛非我道底道理？須知伏䭾尊者五十年中為箇一事，口不敢言，足不敢履。一旦得難提尊者提金剛王寶劒，不犯鋒鋩，直下向咽喉上一刜，直得伏䭾尊者五十年礙膺之物渙然氷釋。所以難提道：汝言與心親，父母非可比。汝行與道合，諸佛心即是。如是則言與心親，則全是本來父母；道與行合，則諸佛之心不從外得。

Senses.Explanation: Yangqi turns Baiyun’s anxiety over his teacher’s laughter into a question about an exorcism performer who welcomes being laughed at. Baiyun Shouduan recites a verse by his earlier teacher, Chaling Yu, to Yangqi Fanghui. Yangqi laughs and walks away, leaving Baiyun troubled through the night. At dawn Yangqi asks whether Baiyun saw the previous day’s exorcism performer. Baiyun says he did, and Yangqi tells him the performer is one step ahead because he likes making people laugh while Baiyun fears their laughter. Baiyun awakens at this explanation. Yinyuan Longqi, Jie’an Jin, Sanshan Denglai, and Dafang Xinghai each retell the encounter and supply a different verse, stressing the laugh, the frightening mask, or the released pearl. The exact question belongs to Yangqi; the four verses are later interpretations of this specific diagnostic turn.

Senses.Explanation: Four teachers challenge a bow or sudden response by asking what understanding it expresses. A layman named Gao asks Yezhu whether he may hear the intent from the West. After Yezhu agrees, the layman bows; Yezhu taps him with a fan and asks the exact question when he declares he will not ask again. At an Xingfu retreat, Hanxiu asks a monk to say his own fundamental matter. After the monk answers that he eats gruel in the morning and is hungry again at night, Hanxiu doubts the response. The monk bows, and Hanxiu demands what he has actually seen before striking him. An older Zhengfayanzang account records Yexian Sheng questioning a monk who suddenly cried out on hearing rain fall from the eaves. The monk answers with a verse on the clear drops and settled mind. In a fourth exchange, layman Xu asks Poshan Haiming for a robe sent by Jin-su. Poshan asks whether Xu understands the meaning beneath the robe threads; when Xu admits he does not but still bows, Poshan asks why and spits when Xu cannot answer. The same question tests a bow, a cry and a claimed understanding in different scenes.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X67/X67n1307.xml). Elder Wansong’s Commentary and Chanted Remarks on Master Tiantong Jue’s Picking Up Ancient Cases: Record of Requests for Instruction. Wansong Xingxiu comments on the case of the Lianhua hermit who raises a staff and asks why earlier worthies will not remain on reaching this point. In explaining it, he identifies the hermit as Xiang of Lianhua Peak, a successor of Fengxian Shen, then quotes Xiang's final address: 'Tell me: when the ancient Buddhas reach here, why are they unwilling to stay?' The teacher Fengxian is part of Xiang's lineage description; he is not the speaker of this question. Wansong adds his own direct answer: 'For fear a dead stump will tether a dull donkey.' That cap makes remaining into attachment to something lifeless. It actively interprets the question rather than simply copying its narrative. Wansong next compares other staff actions, including Shandao's appeal to past, future and present Buddhas, against which he insists that the patriarchs do not act that way. Thus his present intervention warns against making even a revered precedent into a place of confinement.

GrammarEvidence.line: Both passages identify Xiang of Lianhua Peak as master; he is a successor of Fengxian Shen. The following 師臨終 therefore concerns Xiang, not his lineage teacher.
GrammarEvidence.expanded-context: X87 first narrates Xiang recognizing Cong and describes his teaching, then his deathbed staff question and own reply. X67 likewise starts 江州廬山蓮華峰祥庵主...嗣奉先深 and then quotes his terminal address. Wansong道 explicitly marks the later dead-stump cap.
GrammarEvidence.section-header: X67 tenth case Lianhua Does Not Stay. X87 continuous prose anecdote, no new named actor intervenes between Xiang identification and deathbed scene.

席㝡盛，師作燈頭，聞僧眾談泗州僧伽近於楊州出現，有設問者曰：既是泗州大聖，為什麼向楊州出現？聰曰：君子愛財，取之有道。一眾大笑。有僧至蓮華峰祥菴主所，舉似之，祥公大驚曰：雲門兒孫猶在。中夜望雲居拜之，聰之名遂重叢林。祥公，奉先深禪師之嗣，知見甚高，氣壓諸方。甞示眾曰：若是此事，最是急切，須是明取始得。若是明得，時中免被拘繫，便得隨處安閑。亦不要將心捺伏，須是自然合佗古轍去始得。纔到學處分劑，便須露布箇道理，以為佛法幾時得心地休歇去。上座却請與麼相委好。臨終上堂，舉拄杖問眾曰：汝道古佛到這裏，為什麼不肯住？眾莫有對者，乃自曰：為佗途路不得力。復曰：作麼生得力去？橫拄杖肩上曰：楖𣗖橫擔不顧人，却入千峰萬峰去。言訖而化。嗟乎！今之學者，其識趣與前輩何其相遠耶？如祥公聞聰燈頭一語，知其為雲門兒孫，其後莫能逃其言。今雖對面終身論辯，莫辨邪正者有矣。其故何哉？以其臨死生之際，超然自得如此，則其平生所養高妙可知。惜乎！莫有嗣之者。師與西峰雲豁禪師，兄弟也。百丈山第二代法正禪師，大智之高弟。其先甞誦涅槃經，不言姓名，時呼為涅槃和尚。住成法席，師功最多。使眾開田，方說大義者，乃師也。黃蘗、古

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X87/X87n1624.xml). Forest Notes. Huihong's Forest Notes gives the original question within an account of Lianhua Xiang. After describing Xiang's discernment of another monk and his insistence on naturally aligning with the ancient track rather than forcibly suppressing mind, Huihong recounts Xiang's last hall address. He raises his staff and asks why the ancient Buddhas will not stay here. No one answers. Xiang supplies the reply himself: 'Because the road gives them no strength.' He asks how strength is obtained, places the staff across his shoulders and declares that he goes straight among the many peaks without looking back; the narrative says he then dies. The exact question is Xiang's, while Huihong is the later author reporting and admiring his freedom at death. The question and movement refuse a settled endpoint, rather than asking for a geographical explanation. Huihong's admiration is his appraisal of the narrated scene, not independent proof of every biographical detail. Wansong's dead-stump cap is a distinct later reading of this same challenge.

GrammarEvidence.line: Both passages identify Xiang of Lianhua Peak as master; he is a successor of Fengxian Shen. The following 師臨終 therefore concerns Xiang, not his lineage teacher.

Senses.Explanation: Tell me: when the ancient Buddhas reach here, why are they unwilling to stay? Wansong Xingxiu comments on the case of the Lianhua hermit who raises a staff and asks why earlier worthies will not remain on reaching this point. In explaining it, he identifies the hermit as Xiang of Lianhua Peak, a successor of Fengxian Shen, then quotes Xiang's final address: 'Tell me: when the ancient Buddhas reach here, why are they unwilling to stay?' The teacher Fengxian is part of Xiang's lineage description; he is not the speaker of this question. Wansong adds his own direct answer: 'For fear a dead stump will tether a dull donkey.' That cap makes remaining into attachment to something lifeless. It actively interprets the question rather than simply copying its narrative. Wansong next compares other staff actions, including Shandao's appeal to past, future and present Buddhas, against which he insists that the patriarchs do not act that way. Thus his present intervention warns against making even a revered precedent into a place of confinement. Huihong's Forest Notes gives the original question within an account of Lianhua Xiang. After describing Xiang's discernment of another monk and his insistence on naturally aligning with the ancient track rather than forcibly suppressing mind, Huihong recounts Xiang's last hall address. He raises his staff and asks why the ancient Buddhas will not stay here. No one answers. Xiang supplies the reply himself: 'Because the road gives them no strength.' He asks how strength is obtained, places the staff across his shoulders and declares that he goes straight among the many peaks without looking back; the narrative says he then dies. The exact question is Xiang's, while Huihong is the later author reporting and admiring his freedom at death. The question and movement refuse a settled endpoint, rather than asking for a geographical explanation. Huihong's admiration is his appraisal of the narrated scene, not independent proof of every biographical detail. Wansong's dead-stump cap is a distinct later reading of this same challenge.

Senses.Note: Three distinct present verse appraisals of one Nanquan-Zhaozhou encounter are retained. Nanquan speaks the selected conditional sentence; Zhaozhou performs the gesture and the later record hosts write the verses. J28's anthology contains named earlier verses and remains a disclosed reserve, not an additional historical event. The conditional concerns what could have happened before the killing, not a report that the cat was later revived.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB396.xml). Panlong Zisu Chaoyuan quotes the dispute between the two halls, Nanquan's demand for a word to save the cat, the assembly's silence and the killing. When Zhaozhou returns, he hears the case, puts sandals on his head and leaves, eliciting Nanquan's selected response. Zisu's own verse says even that sandal gesture still fails Nanquan's heartfelt intention and that many blind readers miss the tune. His appraisal therefore keeps tension within the apparent approval rather than treating it as a simple final endorsement.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB408.xml). Azi Jinwu quotes the same cat dispute and Nanquan's reply after Zhaozhou's sandal gesture. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Tianyin Yuanxiu quotes the Buddha returning from teaching his mother in heaven. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB410.xml). Lianfeng Su raises the Lotus-Color story at a requested hall sermon. ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Tianyin Yuanxiu quotes the Buddha returning from teaching his mother in heaven. The nun Lotus-Color takes a royal form to arrive before the monks; the Buddha gives the selected rebuke and contrasts her with Subhuti sitting in the rocks. Senses.Explanation: The Buddha's rebuke in the inherited Lotus-Color nun story distinguishes her spectacular arrival from Subhuti's seeing while seated apart. In these records the contrast is material for Zen criticism: the later teachers question the rebuke, the division it draws and the nun's failure to answer back. Tianyin Yuanxiu quotes the Buddha returning from teaching his mother in heaven. The nun Lotus-Color takes a royal form to arrive before the monks; the Buddha gives the selected rebuke and contrasts her with Subhuti sitting in the rocks. Tianyin says she failed to understand this excessive compassion, but also limits the Buddha's handling to tathagata Chan. He would meet the transformed arrival with a blow that prevents further transformation, then gives a sky-and-water reply. The contrast is being tested through his present intervention. Shengren Hanke quotes the same return story, giving forty-nine rather than ninety days in heaven. He asks whether there is a dharma body outside the physical body or a physical body outside the dharma body, accuses the Buddha of deceiving the woman and misrepresenting the monk, and says neither has dreamed of the Buddha's body. His verse contrasts Han Wudi's failed search for immortality with Wang Qiao's ascent. This critique resists turning the selected distinction into a settled definition. Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：祝聖已蒙師指示，向上宗乘事若何？師云：雞知將旦，鶴知夜半。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1366.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wuchu Daguan. An unnamed monk at Wuchu Daguan's inaugural assembly asks first for a teaching amid the imperial summons and ceremonial blessing. Wuchu answers with an iron figure below a golden incense burner. The monk then says the blessing has been explained and asks about the higher matter of the Chan lineage. Wuchu replies that a cock knows approaching dawn and a crane midnight. The repeated question moves the exchange from ceremonial praise to another demand, but the natural timing image does not define a separate secret doctrine. The exact headword belongs to the monk; the cock-and-crane reply belongs to Wuchu.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧云：祝聖已蒙師指示，向上宗乘事若何？答云：六耳不同謀。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1386.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shitian Faxun. At Shitian Faxun's installation, a monk asks how to bless the ruler when the teaching wheel turns. Shitian answers that all appearances cry long life together. The monk raises the headword to request the further matter, and receives 'Six ears do not share the same counsel.' He thanks the teacher and bows. In his ensuing address, Shitian says the transmission is now in his hands yet neither coming nor going alone reveals his footing. The terse reply signals a limit on a third-party account of intimacy; it is not a literal rule forbidding three people to converse.

Senses.Explanation: Casting an iron ox at Shaanfu is an allusive Zen saying, often paired with striking a great elephant at Jiazhou. Shanciji uses the pair to end a verse on the Baizhang wild-fox case. An unnamed monk later asks Maoxi Xingsen what the paired saying means, making the phrase itself the subject of a dialogue. In a separate lamp scene, Yungai Zhi gives the Shaanfu line as a terse answer when a monk asks for another sound. These records show a portable image used to close a verse, invite explanation, or redirect a question; they do not establish a historical account of casting the ox.

Senses.Explanation: The iron ox of Shaanfu is a fixed encounter-image, an immense iron animal set against the great elephant of Jiazhou. Baiyu Jingsi asks about the ox wrestling the elephant, Guxue Zhenzhe asks why it swallowed the elephant, and Liangting Jingting arrays both among other impossible figures in verse. Senses.Explanation: In the Chan corpus this bird is overwhelmingly the goose king that selects milk from water. One instruction gives the image directly: 'there is milk in water; people do not see it; the goose king selects it.' Another says that when water and milk are mixed, the goose king eats the milk. Masters then use the fixed line 'the goose king selects the milk, naturally not of the duck kind' as an appraisal after cases and answers. In a hall exchange an unnamed monk asks the purport of that line and Fenyang Shanzhao answers, 'south of the river there is; north of the river there is not,' without explaining the bird further. Another address pairs capacities: it takes a goose king to select milk and a lion to bite. A verse also reverses the stock contrast: under one strike, 'the goose king becomes a duck; the soft-shelled turtle becomes a tortoise.' The Zen deviation is this legendary bird's repeated use—and deliberate reversal—as a teaching-seat appraisal of selection and discrimination; the entry does not add a hidden object beyond the milk, water, goose, and duck named by the records.

Senses.Explanation: The goose king separates out the milk names the traditional image of distinguishing milk from water. Zhongfeng Mingben explicitly sets water and milk side by side and says the goose king alone can distinguish them. Dahui Zonggao, Tianyin Yuanxiu, and Daxiu Zhu use the phrase, usually with 素非鴨類, as a verdict or answer when asking who can distinguish. The cited passages do not turn that comparison into a general faculty or doctrine.

Senses.Explanation: “The goose king selects milk; it is never of the duck kind” credits discriminating recognition: a capable reader separates what is worth taking from what merely resembles it. Dahui Zonggao uses the verdict in two retained recorded-sayings witnesses to reject a superficial treatment of awakening or to cap a case. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.
